a11_0825650.text: Well, that was good [garble]. Shall we go to maneuver, I mean to sleep attitude - anybody object to doing that?

a11_0825650.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0825650.text: That'd be alright.

a11_0825650.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0825650.text: Okay, I'm ready for you cats to transfer to LM power. What time GET you got?

a11_0825650.speaker: SC
a11_0825650.text: [Very faint and lost in the noise.]

a11_0825650.speaker: Duke
a11_0825650.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Say again. Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0825650.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0825650.text: Get the [garble], Buzz.

a11_0825650.speaker: Collins
a11_0825650.text: ...83 hours. You ready to do it?

a11_0825650.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0825650.text: [Garble].

a11_0825650.speaker: Collins
a11_0825650.text: You ready to do it?

a11_0825650.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0825650.text: Stand by. Yes, go ahead and do it.

a11_0825650.speaker: Collins
a11_0825650.text: Okay.

a11_0825650.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0825650.text: You got 83 hours right now, huh?

a11_0825650.speaker: Collins
a11_0825650.text: Yes, 83 hours, and we're on LM power.

a11_0825650.speaker: Duke
a11_0825650.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We got a lot of noise on the downlink. Would you please try your High Gain in wide beamwidth. The angles are 180 on the yaw, and pitch zero. Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0825650.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0825650.text: Glycol pump.

a11_0825650.speaker: Collins
a11_0825650.text: Houston, Apollo 11. How do you read on the High Gain? Over.

a11_0825650.speaker: Duke
a11_0825650.text: Roger, Mike. You're a lot better now. Over.

a11_0825650.speaker: Collins
a11_0825650.text: Okay. You want it wide beam for some reason?

a11_0825650.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0825650.text: Will you cut my Suit Power and Audio, Off, please?

a11_0825650.speaker: Duke
a11_0825650.text: That's affirmative. We got you in the shadow zone. You're looking right down along the engine bell towards the Earth so we need you in wide beam. Over.

a11_0825650.speaker: Collins
a11_0825650.text: Yes.

a11_0825650.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0825650.text: Okay, going Off now.

a11_0825650.speaker: Collins
a11_0825650.text: Okay. Fine. We're starting our maneuver to sleep attitude. Roll 82, pitch 229, yaw zero.

a11_0825650.speaker: Duke
a11_0825650.text: Roger. The angles you got in the Flight Plan will be good when you get there.

a11_0825650.speaker: Collins
a11_0825650.text: About ready to maneuver?

a11_0825650.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0825650.text: Go ahead.

a11_0825650.speaker: Collins
a11_0825650.text: Okay.

a11_0825650.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0825650.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; at 83 hours, 2 minutes into the flight of Apollo 11. Currently we show an apolune of 65.3 nautical miles [120.9 km], a perilune of 53.9 [99.8 km]. We would expect the transfer to Lunar Module power to occur momentarily and from that point on, the communications check with the Lunar Module. 83 hours, 3 minutes and standing by; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a11_0825650.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0825650.text: Yes?

a11_0825650.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0825650.text: You're past step 4?

a11_0825650.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0825650.text: Houston, 11.

a11_0825650.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0825650.text: What's the page?

a11_0825650.speaker: Duke
a11_0825650.text: Go ahead, 11. Over.

a11_0825650.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0825650.text: Okay. We're on page Activation 12 and 13, at step 4, and verify descent talkbacks gray, and they're barber-pole.

a11_0825650.speaker: Duke
a11_0825650.text: Roger. Stand by. [Pause.]

a11_0825650.speaker: Duke
a11_0825650.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We'd like you to put - take the low voltage taps Off, Reset, then On. Over.

a11_0825650.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0825650.text: Stand by. We've got it. We've just had - one circuit breaker out of position.

a11_0825650.speaker: Duke
a11_0825650.text: Okay.

a11_0825650.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0825650.text: We have them gray now.

a11_0825650.speaker: Duke
a11_0825650.text: Rog.

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: A lot of static - on the Command Module S-band.

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: Well, we - we should still have him.

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Radio check on S-band.

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: I'm not getting them on...

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: Well, we're almost at sleep attitude. Just stand by one, and, as soon as we get there, I'll find out where they are. I'm going to dick with the DAP right now.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: [Garble] should have warmed up by now. [Long pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: I've got nothing but static.

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Oh, he's transmitting on B.

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: Hey, Mike, you transmitting on B? [Long pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: Mike, what are you transmitting on up there?

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: Say again.

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: What are you transmitting on up there?

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: I'm transmitting right now on Omni A, but I'm about to get new High Gain angles. Just 1 second. Okay, we're there.

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: How come I - he don't hear you on Intercom?

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: You should hear...

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Houston, Apollo 11 - Apollo 11, Eagle. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Roger, Eagle. This is Houston. We read you. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Roger. I read you about four-by-four. Could you give me a short count, please?

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: Geezes, I don't hear him.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Roger, Eagle. Coming in with the short count - 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Houston out. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0830700.text: That was Buzz Aldrin from the Lunar Module using the codename for the first time.

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: We don't read them, Buzz.

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: He's - he's on LM S-band, Neil, apparently.

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: Oh.

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: Yes.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Roger. Are you copying my Low Bit Rate? Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Rog. We got some beautiful data here, Eagle. We're - All those guys are looking at it - systems guys. We'll have some word for you in a minute how everything looks.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Roger. I'm all ready to switch to High Bit Rate, if that's okay with you.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Would you please stand by, Eagle. We want to get to the proper sleep attitude before we proceed on with the comm check. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Standing by. [Pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Houston, Eagle. We'll go ahead with the camera check-out. I'm still on low taps, and I assume there's no problem doing that. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Stand by.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: That's affirmative. No problem on that, Eagle. You can go ahead and power up the sequence camera. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: Houston, Columbia. How do you read on the High Gain?

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Should have done that before.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Eagle, be advised - sounds like a hot mike. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Right. Yes. [Pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: Did you hear him answer?

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: No.

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: I didn't either. Buzz is reading him, though.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Roger. If you're reading me now, I am in hot mike because I'm in ICS push-to-talk, and Downvoice Backup. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Roger. We just wanted to remind you. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Thank you. [Long pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Columbia, this is Houston. Are you maneuvering to sleep attitude? Over. [Pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Eagle, this is Houston. We have lost all our voice and data with Columbia. Would you see if he is maneuvering to sleep attitude? Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: Houston, Columbia. How do you read on the High Gain? Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Hey, Mike. You maneuvering to sleep attitude? [Pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: Hey, how about asking them if they can hear me calling?

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: I don't believe they can hear you, Mike. Are you maneuvering now to sleep attitude? [Pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: Well, we're in sleep attitude, and I got the High Gain angles, and they should be good angles. And I'm locked on and I got about a half signal strength, and they can't hear me.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Houston, Eagle. The Columbia has maneuvered to sleep attitude. He's got the High Gain Antenna's - antenna angles set in, and he should be communicating with you. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Roger. We don't have him. Stand by.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Eagle, Houston. Would you please have Columbia hit Command Reset? Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: No go.

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: What'd he say?

a11_0830700.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0830700.text: Wilco. Command Reset. [Pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: Okay.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Eagle, Houston. Since we're in sleep attitude, I'll give you another long count. If you're reading in this mode, we'd like you to switch to high bit rate. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: [Garble] try him again.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Roger. Go ahead with your short count.

a11_0830700.speaker: Collins
a11_0830700.text: Houston, Columbia. Reading you loud and clear.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Roger. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. We're reading you five-by. You can go to high bit rate now. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Roger. Going to high bit rate now. [Long pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Eagle, this is Houston. Do you read? Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Houston, this is Eagle. Roger. Read you loud and clear. How me? Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Roger. Reading you five-by also, Buzz, and we got the high bit rate. It's looking beautiful through Goldstone. Giving you a count: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Please give us a count. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Roger, Houston. Eagle with a count. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Roger. Stand by. We're reading you five-by. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Okay. I'm ready to go S-band voice. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Stand by, Eagle. Stand by on step 4. [Long pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0830700.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. A voice count exchange between Buzz Aldrin in the Eagle, the Lunar Module, and Charles Duke here in Mission Control Center.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Columbia, this is Houston. Would you please give us P00 and Accept. We've got a load for you. Break. Eagle, we are ready to go to step 4. Please select S-band Voice to Voice. Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Hello, Eagle. This is Houston. How do you read - normal voice? Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Eagle - Houston, this is Eagle. Read you loud and clear on S-band, normal voice. How me? Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Rog. You're beautiful in this mode, Buzz. We're reading you five-by. Coming with a short count and we'd like one back from you. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Houston out.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Roger. Houston, Eagle. You're gorgeous also. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Eagle, over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Roger, Eagle. This is better than the downvoice backup. Stand by one. [Long pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Eagle, Houston. Everybody's happy as a clam with this mode. We'd like to stay here for a little bit. Telemetry looks great, and the voice is great. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Roger. Understand. I'm checking out camera number 4 now. [Long pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0830700.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. Our communications checkout with the Eagle apparently going very well at this time.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Eagle, Houston. Say again what you're checking out? Over. [Pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Roger, Houston. Eagle has checked out both 70-millimeter cameras and both 16-millimeter cameras, and all work fine. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Sounds great. Stand by. [Pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Eagle, Houston. We've looked over your systems on the high bit rate. Everything looks super; we're ready to go. Over. [Pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Roger. Stand by. You want to go back to low bit rate now?

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Stand by on that. Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Eagle, Houston. We look good through the 210 on this mode. We're going to shift data select to an 85-foot dish to see what we got, and then we'll be back to you on the 210. If you'll stand by a couple of minutes in this mode, we'll be back with you. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Roger. Eagle standing by. [Long pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0830700.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. 83 hours, 21 minutes now into the flight. Meanwhile, aboard the Eagle, apparently Buzz Aldrin and Neil Armstrong although Buzz is doing most of the comm check at this time.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Eagle, Houston. How do you read? Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Houston, Eagle. Read you loud and clear. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Roger. We're reading you five-by. We've got the voice good through the 85. The telemetry is in and out through the 85. Stand by. We'll be back through you - with you through the 210. Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Eagle, Houston. You can go step 5 now. We'd like low bit rate. Over. [Pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Houston, Eagle. You have low bit rate.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Roger. Copy, Eagle. [Long pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Eagle, Houston. Could you give me a short count - this mode? Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0830700.text: Houston, this is Eagle with a short count. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Eagle. Over.

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: Roger, Eagle. You're five-by. This S-band voice is really beautiful. Over. [Pause.]

a11_0830700.speaker: Duke
a11_0830700.text: And, Eagle, Houston. We'll be standing in - standing by in this mode for a minute or so. We'll be back with you if you'll just stand by. Over. [Pause.]

a11_0832526.speaker: Duke
a11_0832526.text: Eagle, this is Houston coming through the 210. How do you read? Over.

a11_0832526.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0832526.text: Roger. Read you loud and clear. [Long pause.]

a11_0832526.speaker: Duke
a11_0832526.text: Eagle, this is Houston. We're happy with all our data in all modes. You can power down the comm now. Over.

a11_0832526.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0832526.text: Roger. Understand. Eagle will power down the comm, and we're just approaching 27 volts now. Looks like we won't have to bother with the high taps.

a11_0832526.speaker: Duke
a11_0832526.text: Columbia, this is Houston. We got a TEI-11 PAD for you and an update on the water dump. Over.

a11_0832526.speaker: Collins
a11_0832526.text: Stand by one, Houston. Are you through with the DSKY?

a11_0832526.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0832526.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 83 hours and 27 minutes now into the flight, Apollo 11. That last exchange between Charlie Duke, our capsule communicator, and Buzz Aldrin aboard the Eagle, identifying that we're very well satisfied with the communications check on the Lunar Module and will proceed with powering down the spacecraft. At 83 hours, 27 minutes; we now read an altitude of 54.3 nautical miles [100.6 km], a velocity of 5,376 feet per second [1,639 m/s]. This is Apollo Control, Houston.

a11_0832925.speaker: Collins
a11_0832925.text: Houston, Columbia. Ready to copy TEI-11. Over.

a11_0832925.speaker: Duke
a11_0832925.text: Rog, Columbia. Here we come with the TEI-11. SPS/G&N: 37200; minus 0.60, plus 0.47. Noun 33, 098:05:24.22; plus 4144.8, plus 0371.9, minus 0242.2. Roll is NA; pitch, 020; the rest of the PAD is NA. Set stars are NA. The ullage is two quads - correction, two jets for 16 seconds; use Bravo and Delta. In the comments, the undocked present CSM - correction, this is for - TEI-11 is undocked. Present onboard weight of the CSM is 37,200 pounds, about 50 Alpha on your DAP. Over.

a11_0832925.speaker: Collins
a11_0832925.text: All right. I read back TEI-11. SPS G&N: 37200; minus 0.60, plus 0.47. Plus 098:05:24.22, plus 4144.8, plus 0371.9, minus 0242.2. NA, 020; the rest of the PAD NA. Ullage, two jets for 16 seconds, Quads B and D. Undocked. Present CSM weight is okay in the DAP.

a11_0832925.speaker: Duke
a11_0832925.text: Roger, 11. And we'd like you to do a waste-water dump at 84 hours down to 25 percent. Over. [Pause.]

a11_0832925.speaker: Collins
a11_0832925.text: Roger. Understand. Waste-water dump to 25 percent at 84 hours.

a11_0832925.speaker: Duke
a11_0832925.text: Roger. And, Mike, we'll have LOS in about 11 minutes at 83:44. AOS is 84:30, and prior to - or at LOS, we would like you to go - Configure the S-band for High Gain track to Reacq, High Gain Beam to Narrow, and let's try that to see if we can get an automatic Reacq at the next AOS. Over.

a11_0832925.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0832925.text: That was Mike Collins, aboard Columbia, taking down a maneuver PAD.

a11_0832925.speaker: Collins
a11_0832925.text: I'm in Reacq and Narrow now.

a11_0832925.speaker: Duke
a11_0832925.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Also, that water that you got on the aft bulkhead, we - If it's not too much, we just recommend sopping it up and then throwing the sponges away in the waste wat - in the waste stowage area. If it's too much, then we use - recommend using the procedure in the checklist on page F 10-14. Over.

a11_0832925.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0832925.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 83 hours, 34 minutes now into the flight, Apollo 11. The Lunar Module communications has - has been deactivated. We currently show a velocity of 5,377 feet per second [1,639 m/s]. Our orbital parameters now read 65.1 nautical miles [120.6 km] apolune, 54.2 nautical miles [100.4 km] perilune. At 84 hours, 35 minutes, continuing to follow. This is Apollo Control, Houston.

a11_0833725.speaker: Duke
a11_0833725.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Would you have Buzz make sure he gives us the OPS pressure readings before you close up? Over.

a11_0833725.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0833725.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 83 hours, 40 minutes now into the flight, Apollo 11. We're less than 4 minutes away now from time of Loss Of Signal with the Apollo 11 spacecraft. At the present time our velocity reading; 5,375 feet per second [1,638 m/s]. Our total weight in orbit at this time, reading 70,502 pounds [31,979 kg]. Our orbital parameters: apolune, 65.1 nautical miles [120.6 km]; perilune, 54.2 nautical miles [100.4 km]. This is Apollo Control, Houston.

a11_0833725.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0833725.text: Houston, 11. The OPS's read 5,750, both bottles.

a11_0833725.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0833725.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 83 hours, 38 minutes. Apollo 11 now on CSM power.

a11_0834000.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0834000.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; at 83 hours, 43 minutes now into the flight, Apollo 11. Less than a minute away from predicted time of Loss Of Signal with the Apollo 11 spacecraft. We expect the next time we acquire Apollo 11, its crew; Neil Armstrong, Mike Collins and Buzz Aldrin; will have begun their rest period. And at 83 hours, 43 minutes; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a11_0834300.speaker: Collins
a11_0834300.text: Armstrong says it's the hatch and - if we leave the probe and drogue there, we'll save us some time tomorrow. I don't know if it's tolerable sleeping or not. I think what previous crews have been doing is re-installing all that claptrap up in there.

a11_0834300.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0834300.text: Apollo 11 has passed out of range with the ground, traversing now over the far side of the Moon. During this pass, we had an extremely successful communications checkout with the Lunar Module using its code name for the first time, its code name of the Eagle. Buzz Aldrin performed the counting tasks in concert with Charlie Duke, the Capsule Communicator here on the ground, and at times Buzz's - in Buzz's voice, we noted considerable enthusiasm for the way things are going, and at times Charlie Duke shared that enthusiasm. And its maiden checkout in communications, the Lunar Module Eagle looked

a11_0834300.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0834300.text: I don't think that would be too horrible sleeping down there.

a11_0834300.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0834300.text: It's for sure it's not going anywhere; this one's bolted down two places - and this one is...

a11_0834300.speaker: Collins
a11_0834300.text: You can try it. If we could find a place to put our legs back in there, it'll be alright.

a11_0842800.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0842800.text: Mark. 30 seconds now from time of scheduled acquisition.

a11_0842800.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0842800.text: Mark. 20 seconds. 10 seconds. We should be acquiring shortly and we're standing by.

a11_0842800.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0842800.text: We have - have data. We've acquired data on Apollo 11.

a11_0842800.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0842800.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. Owen Garriott getting ready to place a call.

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Over.

a11_0842800.speaker: Collins
a11_0842800.text: Houston, Apollo 11.

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: 11, Houston. Roger. Reading you fine, and it looks like the automatic Reacq went very well just as soon as you came around the limb. We have several small items to discuss with you here just before you go to sleep. Over.

a11_0842800.speaker: Collins
a11_0842800.text: Go ahead, Owen.

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: Okay, 11. First of all, on our LM systems checks, everything went fine. I would like to remind you, though, tomorrow you may see an ascent pressure light when you activate the MC&W. There should be no problem, however. You did note that the APS Aux tank pressure was only reading 111 psi, which is normal at this point, but below the level which will trigger your light due to the helium which has been dissolved into the propellant. Over.

a11_0842800.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0842800.text: Roger. Understand that. Thank you.

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: Roger. And next item, the supercritical helium rise rate is nominal, and you also had that question for us about your thruster activity during the P22 on the last rev. Believe we understand that now, as you reported that your pitch was in Accel Command and your yaw and roll were in Rate Command. You were firing your pitch thrusters. This will couple rates into your yaw and roll axes, and the - You were at that time holding only half a degree deadband and coupling rates into yaw and roll produced the extra firings about the yaw and roll axes. Over.

a11_0842800.speaker: Collins
a11_0842800.text: Yeah, that may be true. It's very peculiar coupling, in that it waits longer than you would think and its reaction is greater than you would think. We were getting yaw rates of around four-tenths of a degree per second, for example.

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: Roger, Mike. We did play the data back, and that's the way it looked upon analysis of the chart recordings back here. Over.

a11_0842800.speaker: Collins
a11_0842800.text: Okay. Fine.

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: They've also looked at the result of your landmark tracking. The marks all apparently were very good, and we've got a full page of data here relative to the altitudes of the various site locations, which I won't read up to you, but I did want to let you know that the marks apparently went very well. I also have your consumable budgets, particularly your RCS propellant quantities. They're Deltas from nominal if you should want them. Your worst quad is quad Charlie, which is 9 percent low. I'll not read up the others unless you want them. Over.

a11_0842800.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0842800.text: Okay. How about the O 2 fuel cell purge? You want that now?

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: I'll have to stand by just a moment.

a11_0842800.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0842800.text: Okay. And then the other one is, we're still charging Battery A. [Long pause.]

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: 11, Houston. We would like to delay the fuel cell purge until the backside of the Moon, and you go ahead and - should terminate your battery charge at this time. Over.

a11_0842800.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0842800.text: Okay. Understand. I knew we had another O 2 and H 2 purge coming up in the morning. I wasn't sure whether you wanted to go through with this one or not. I'll wait until the backside and then do it.

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: That's fine, Buzz.

a11_0842800.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0842800.text: Terminate battery charging now.

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: That's right, and one other systems item here - in order to balance your cryo tanks, would you get your O 2 Tank 1 and your H 2 Tank 2 heaters off? Over. [Pause.]

a11_0842800.speaker: Collins
a11_0842800.text: Okay. I have O 2 Tank Heater 1 off, and H 2 Tank Heater 2 off.

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: That's right, Mike, and we believe you have your quad Bravo and quad Charlie turned off in your DAP at this time, and a 5-degree deadband. We'd prefer a 10-degree deadband for your sleep period overnight, here. Over.

a11_0842800.speaker: Collins
a11_0842800.text: Okay.

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: One other item relative to a malfunction procedure. It's unlikely that you'll have to worry about this tomorrow, but in your malfunction list under docking on page F11-9, there is a malfunction procedure for a high O 2 flow rate at the top of - under tunnel, at the top of page 11-9. We would like to have you not use that malfunction procedure should you encounter the high O 2 flow rate, and instead, check back with Houston for a revised procedure should you find that situation. Over.

a11_0842800.speaker: Collins
a11_0842800.text: Understand, and note has been made in my checklist. [Pause.]

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: 11, Houston. Roger. That just about takes care of all the items we have here on the ground before time to hit the sack, and I guess you will have a pre-sleep check for us before you go to bed. [Pause.]

a11_0842800.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0842800.text: Rog. We're in the midst of cycling the O 2 and H 2 fans now.

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: Roger. [Pause.]

a11_0842800.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0842800.text: And the radiation is as follows: CDR, 11012; CMP, 10013; LMP, 09015. Negative medication. Over.

a11_0842800.speaker: Garriott
a11_0842800.text: Roger. Copy, 11.

a11_0842800.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0842800.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 84 hours, 39 minutes now into the flight. That conversational exchange with Owen Garriott, here in Mission Control Center, and principally Buzz Aldrin. However, Mike Collins did talk briefly about Program 22, the landmark tracking activity in which he performed. At 84 hours, 40 minutes; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a11_0844154.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0844154.text: Roger. We're thinking about taking the monocular with us on into the LM. We think it might prove to be of some use. Over.

a11_0844154.speaker: Garriott
a11_0844154.text: Roger, Buzz. It sounds like a good idea for some of your surveying work there inside the cockpit. Over.

a11_0844154.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0844154.text: Okay. You want to run that by with whoever might be concerned?

a11_0844154.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0844154.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 84 hours, 44 minutes now into the flight, Apollo 11. Our current spacecraft altitude, now 64.3 nautical miles [119.1 km] with an apolune of 65.2 nautical miles [120.8 km]; perilune, 54.4 nautical miles [100.7 km]. We show an orbital period of 1 hour, 58 minutes, 40 seconds on our displays. Current weight of the spacecraft in orbit; 70,502 pounds [31,979 kg]. At 84 hours, 44 minutes, continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a11_0844747.speaker: Garriott
a11_0844747.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We've apparently lost the High Gain lock. We would appreciate it if you would give us a help manually to try to re-lock up on the High Gain. Over.

a11_0844747.speaker: Garriott
a11_0844747.text: 11, Houston. Reading you very weak, still too far down in the noise to complete the full transmission. If you'd give us a hand on a manual relock, we'd appreciate it.

a11_0844747.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0844747.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 84 hours, 48 minutes now into the flight. We're receiving noisy data at this time. We're - have requested Apollo 11 to give us a manual relock. Standing by at 84 hours, 49 minutes; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a11_0845202.speaker: Garriott
a11_0845202.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We're still unable to pick you up on the High Gain Antenna. Request you go to Manual, and Wide Beamwidth. The pitch and yaw angles in your checklist are good ones. You should be able to find us there. Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0845202.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0845202.text: Houston, Apollo 11. How do you read now?

a11_0845202.speaker: Garriott
a11_0845202.text: 11, Houston. Loud and clear this time. How me?

a11_0845202.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0845202.text: Loud and clear. You faded out on your last transmission. Over.

a11_0845202.speaker: Garriott
a11_0845202.text: Roger. Are you in wide beam now?

a11_0845202.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0845202.text: Negative. I got you locked back on again, Reacq and Narrow.

a11_0845202.speaker: Garriott
a11_0845202.text: Rog. That's all we want. We want to stay in Narrow, and we're a little puzzled about why we lost you here a few minutes ago. Do you have any ideas? [Pause.]

a11_0845202.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0845202.text: No, we sure don't [cough] - sure don't. We're showing - we're showing about 15 degrees plus pitch and about 270. That ought to be good and clear.

a11_0845202.speaker: Garriott
a11_0845202.text: We concur there. We still don't have any good ideas on why we were lost. [Long pause.]

a11_0845202.speaker: Garriott
a11_0845202.text: 11, Houston. Would you confirm that we did acquire automatically when you came around the limb for this passage. Over. [Pause.]

a11_0845202.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0845202.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 84 hours, 56 minutes now into the flight, Apollo 11. Our current apolune, 65.1 nautical miles. Current perilune, 54.3 nautical miles. After receiving some noisy signal, Apollo 11 has locked back on in fine form. That was Buzz Aldrin speaking with Owen Garriott here in the Mission Control Center. I expect we will take a second look at why we had to lock on manually. As we receive any updates on this, we'll pass them along. We now read 84 hours, 57 minutes; and this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a11_0850438.speaker: Garriott
a11_0850438.text: 11, Houston. On your Auto RCS Select switches, we show quad Bravo disabled but quad Charlie only partially disabled. Charlie 3, I believe, is the only one you have selected Off. Is that correct? [Pause.]

a11_0850438.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0850438.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 85 hours, 5 minutes now into the flight, Apollo 11. We confirm from the ground, following that conversational exchange, [pause.] as was pointed out...

a11_0850438.speaker: Collins
a11_0850438.text: How do they look to you now, Houston?

a11_0850438.speaker: Garriott
a11_0850438.text: 11, Houston. We see them all disabled at this time. Thank you.

a11_0850438.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0850438.text: ...as was pointed out, quad - RCS quad Charlie is now disabled following that conversational exchange between Owen Garriott and Buzz Aldrin. Buzz, the Lunar Module Pilot apparently, quite obviously still awake. 85 hours, 7 minutes now into the flight, Apollo 11, continuing to monitor; this is Apollo Control, Houston.

a11_0850922.speaker: Garriott
a11_0850922.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Over. [Pause.]

a11_0850922.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0850922.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a11_0850922.speaker: Garriott
a11_0850922.text: 11, Houston. We're going to try to check out this ability to automatically reacquire on the S-band, and what we want to do is to secure our uplink carrier for about 30 seconds. Then we will turn it back on and see if the spacecraft equipment will automatically reacquire. So if you do not get a call from us within about 3 minutes, that means we have not been able to reacquire and request your assistance on a manual acquisition. Over.

a11_0850922.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0850922.text: Okay. We understand.

a11_0850922.speaker: Garriott
a11_0850922.text: 11, Houston. We also would appreciate, if you will note the angles that the antenna tracks through in its attempt to reacquire. Over. [Pause.]

a11_0850922.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0850922.text: Roger. We'll do that.

a11_0850922.speaker: Collins
a11_0850922.text: I have a bit of fruitcake left over from somewhere. If anybody wants some, here it is. [Garble].

a11_0850922.speaker: Collins
a11_0850922.text: Let's have a little chewing gum. Anybody like some chewing gum?

a11_0850922.speaker: SC
a11_0850922.text: 43 [garble].

a11_0850922.speaker: Garriott
a11_0850922.text: 11, Houston. It looks like we're locked back up again with no delay. How does it look on board? Over.

a11_0850922.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0850922.text: Roger. The signal strength dropped very rapidly to zero; and the pitch and yaw, in about 3 seconds, moved toward 40 degrees pitch and 240 degrees yaw. Right now, they're sitting on about 15 degrees pitch and, oh, about 265 degrees yaw. So they didn't move very far, about 30 degrees apiece; and then they picked right back on up again. Over.

a11_0850922.speaker: Garriott
a11_0850922.text: Roger. Some of The Luckiest People in the background there. We copied your pitch and yaw angles.

a11_0850922.speaker: Garriott
a11_0850922.text: 11, Houston. Could you give us the location of your - pitch and yaw location of your position indicators? Over.

a11_0850922.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0850922.text: Roger. They're in the same position as the antenna right now; plus 15 degrees pitch and [pause] - Now, no, wait a minute. I got them - got it at about 275 instead of 265.

a11_0850922.speaker: Garriott
a11_0850922.text: Okay. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a11_0850922.speaker: Garriott
a11_0850922.text: 11, Houston. We'd like to try the same procedure once more. We'll leave the carrier off a little longer and be back up for a call within 4 minutes. Over.

a11_0850922.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0850922.text: Okay.

a11_0850922.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0850922.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 85 hours, 17 minutes now into the flight, Apollo 11. What you heard in the conversation between Owen Garriott and Buzz Aldrin was following a - a communications check in which we secured the uplink carrier for some 30 seconds and waited to give it a period of time of approximately 3 minutes, to see if the spacecraft would reacquire. We appeared to reacquire in fine form on this first test. We will repeat it - this test a second time, delaying approximately 4 minutes before we place a call to Apollo 11. At 85 hours, 17 minutes, we currently read an altitude - sp

a11_0850922.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0850922.text: ...1,000 pounds - [garble].

a11_0850922.speaker: Collins
a11_0850922.text: That'll bring some more junk back here.

a11_0850922.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0850922.text: Couldn't have done better myself.

a11_0850922.speaker: Garriott
a11_0850922.text: 11, Houston. We're locked back up again. Can you give us a report on how the antenna behaved? [Long pause.]

a11_0850922.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0850922.text: Roger. It was essentially identical as before. The pitch went to 45, 40 to 45 and the yaw went to about - to about 255, 245 to 255. And then it rather quickly locked up at 15 degrees pitch and 270 yaw. Over.

a11_0850922.speaker: Garriott
a11_0850922.text: 11, Houston. Roger. Your angles are 45 and 255. Do I understand that as soon as the carrier dropped, it went to these angles? Or did it only go to these angles after the uplink carrier was re-enabled and the antenna began to hunt - to re-acquire? Over.

a11_0850922.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0850922.text: No. As soon as the carrier dropped off, why, it drifted over to those angles and stayed there. Then when it came back up again, why, it hunted around for a while, but didn't get any further off. Gradually brought it on in to the angles where it is right now; and then the signal strength would take several jumps as evidently it goes from Wide to Medium to Narrow. Over.

a11_0850922.speaker: Garriott
a11_0850922.text: 11, Houston. Understand. And on another subject, request you zero your optics for the night. Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0850922.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0850922.text: Roger. Zeroed.

a11_0850922.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0850922.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; at 85 hours, 27 minutes now into the flight, Apollo 11. We've run two tests thus far with the S-band antenna which has reacquired nicely on both occasions. We're standing by for further possible conversations with the crew at this time. We're some 15 minutes from predicted time of Loss Of Signal on Apollo 11. Currently we read an apolune of 65 nautical miles [120.4 km], a perilune of 54.4 nautical miles [100.7 km]. This is Apollo Control, Houston.

a11_0852700.speaker: Garriott
a11_0852700.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Can you confirm that you have changed the CO 2 filter as per Flight Plan in the last hour? Over?

a11_0852700.speaker: Collins
a11_0852700.text: No. We're still eating. We're about to do it. We'll let you know.

a11_0852700.speaker: Garriott
a11_0852700.text: Roger, 11. And we've got about 14 minutes to LOS. AOS is 86:30, an hour away. We're wondering whether or not you plan to have one man up at that time or would you all like to be asleep inside the next hour? Over.

a11_0852700.speaker: Garriott
a11_0852700.text: Roger. The thing that we're still puzzling on is the antenna, and if - as long as there will be somebody up - why, we would like to have somebody check the automatic Reacq on the next AOS.

a11_0852700.speaker: Collins
a11_0852700.text: Okay. We'll do that. We haven't chlorinated the water yet, and we haven't changed the lithium hydroxide. We're just still finishing up dinner.

a11_0852700.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0852700.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 85 hours, 29 minutes now into the flight. That was Mike Collins reporting to Capsule Communicator Owen Garriott that the Apollo 11 crew completing dinner at this time. And earlier perhaps, as you listened to the air/ground, you heard some music in the background, soft music which would indicate that the this was being played in concert with their evening meal. When we reacquire, we expect one of the three crew members to still be, at least one to be still awake as we run a further check on our spacecraft antenna. At 85 hours, 30 minutes into the flight of Apoll

a11_0854005.speaker: Garriott
a11_0854005.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We have LOS coming up in 2 minutes now, and AOS will be at 86 plus 28 plus 15. Over.

a11_0854005.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0854005.text: We'll see you on the other side, Houston.

a11_0854005.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0854005.text: 85 hours, 40 minutes at this time. That - perhaps the last conversation we'll have with Apollo 11 until we reacquire. We're now 1 minute, 20 seconds away from Loss Of Signal. Continuing to stand by; this is Apollo Control, Houston at 85 hours, 41 minutes.

a11_0854005.speaker: Collins
a11_0854005.text: I guess what I'm doing, I should do with the paper towels.

a11_0854005.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0854005.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston. We've had Loss Of Signal as the Apollo 11 spacecraft begins its pass around the far side of the Moon at 85 hours, 42 minutes.

a11_0862615.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0862615.text: Mark. One minute from predicted Acquisition Of Signal.

a11_0862615.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0862615.text: Are we going to keep the... lens on?

a11_0862615.speaker: Collins
a11_0862615.text: [Garble] getting earlier in time. Yes, that's best - better.

a11_0862615.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0862615.text: We should be acquiring. We're standing by.

a11_0862615.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0862615.text: Got a Master Alarm coming on here.

a11_0862615.speaker: Collins
a11_0862615.text: Good deal. Keep working, you got a lot of film.

a11_0862615.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0862615.text: Yes, I guess so. Nothing like filming your [garble].

a11_0862615.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0862615.text: [Garble] this field of view, it's mostly just blues. I keep getting mostly black and blue.

a11_0862615.speaker: Garriott
a11_0862615.text: 11, Houston. Loud and clear here. Over.

a11_0862615.speaker: Collins
a11_0862615.text: Okay. We just appeared to get a solid lock for the last - oh, about a minute. The Tune-for-Max needles have been wandering up and down, and the pitch and yaw needles have been wandering around, but it appears to have reacquired by itself solidly now. We're just filling - finishing up our fuel cell purge. Hydrogen on number 3 is the last to go Off, and it'll be coming Off just in a second.

a11_0862615.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0862615.text: Huh? Is that right? Really should have looked.

a11_0862615.speaker: Garriott
a11_0862615.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We believe we've tracked down the reacquisition problem we had on the previous rev. It looks like it was a receiver power supply here on the ground and no problems in the spacecraft at all. Over.

a11_0862615.speaker: Garriott
a11_0862615.text: 11, that really winds things up as far as we're concerned on the ground, for the evening. We're ready to go to bed and get a little sleep. Over.

a11_0862615.speaker: Collins
a11_0862615.text: Yeah. We're about to join you.

a11_0862615.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0862615.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; 86 hours, 33 minutes. You heard that last exchange. The Mission Control Center has isolated our earlier loss of lock-on with the S-Band antenna to a faulty power supply at Goldstone which in turn introduced noisy data causing a ground-based receiver to go out of lock. This power supply, a 24-volt one, has already been replaced at Goldstone. In summary, the spacecraft looks good and the difficulty was caused here on the ground. At 86 hours, 34 minutes; we now read our orbit at 64.9 nautical miles [120.2 km] apolune, 54.6 nautical miles [101.1 km] perilune. This

a11_0865200.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0865200.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston; at 87 hours, 31 minutes now into the flight, Apollo 11. The Apollo 11 spacecraft continues on its front-side pass above the Moon. We're now less than 10 minutes away from the Loss Of Signal. The Apollo 11 crew in - currently in their rest period. We've received no indication yet that any of the three crew members are actually sleeping, although all three appear to be in a very restful mode. This will be the final sleep period for the crew, now at the threshold of their prime mission objective, for the final sleep period prior to landing on the lunar surface and

a11_0873100.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0873100.text: This is Apollo Control, Houston at 87 hours, 40 minutes now into the flight, Apollo 11. Apollo 11 now less than a minute away from Loss Of Signal as it is due to pass over the far side of the Moon and out of range with the Mission Control Center, as well as the rest of the world. We've had no further conversations with the crew. All spacecraft systems appear in fine shape. We're now less than 30 seconds away from our time of Loss Of Signal and standing by.

a11_0874000.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0874000.text: We've had Loss Of Signal as Apollo 11 passes over the backside of the Moon.

a11_0874000.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0874000.text: This is Apollo Control; 89 hours, 38 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Coming down - actually, we've had Loss Of Signal on this, the seventh lunar revolution of Apollo 11. Should have acquisition again at 90 hours, 25 minutes through the Honeysuckle Creek, Australia station. The crew has been asleep about 2 hours, a little over 2 hours when the third man finally went to sleep, Mike Collins, after a brief interchange with the ground. And 3 hours, 57 minutes remaining in the sleep period. Cabin pressure now holding at 4.7 pounds per square inch [32.4 kPa] at a temperature of 69 degrees Fahrenheit [20

a11_0893800.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0893800.text: This is Apollo Control; 91 hours, 36 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Less than 1 minute remaining until Loss Of Signal with Apollo 11 as it goes onto the lunar far side in the eighth lunar revolution. Two hours remaining in the crew rest period, which means that midway through the next front-side pass the crew will be wakened, if they're not indeed already awake. Flight Surgeon Ken Beers reported, just prior to LOS in a brief exchange here in Mission Control, that the crew apparently were all asleep soundly at this time. Flight Director Glynn Lunney asked the spacecraft systems engineers how the

a11_0913600.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0913600.text: This is Apollo Control; 93 hours, 29 minutes Ground Elapsed Time. Some 5 minutes away from Loss Of Signal on the Apollo 11 on this revolution. A wake-up call is expected from spacecraft communicator Ron Evans here in Mission Control just prior to the time the spacecraft goes into the - goes over the hill on the lunar far side. Standing by as we wait for him to make his call. Presently, Apollo 11 is in an orbit measuring 64 nautical miles [118.5 km] at apocynthion, 55.5 nautical miles [102.8 km] at pericynthion. Present orbital velocity around the Moon, 5,370 feet per second [1,637 m/s]. Spacec

a11_0932900.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0932900.text: Still standing by for the wake-up call.

a11_0932900.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0932900.text: Standing by for Ron Evans' big moment as he makes his call to the spacecraft, as being the sleep watch, his job has been rather easy or at least he hasn't had too much conversation with... Here we go.

a11_0932900.speaker: Evans
a11_0932900.text: Apollo 11, Apollo 11. Good morning from the Black Team. [Long pause.]

a11_0932900.speaker: Evans
a11_0932900.text: Good morning. We got about 2 minutes to LOS here, Mike.

a11_0932900.speaker: Evans
a11_0932900.text: (Laughing) Yeah, you're about 2 minutes early here on the wake-up. Looks like you're really sawing them away.

a11_0932900.speaker: Evans
a11_0932900.text: 11, Houston. For planning purposes, you can go ahead and take the monocular into the LM with you.

a11_0932900.speaker: Collins
a11_0932900.text: Okay. I'll tell them. How are all the CSM systems looking? [Pause.]

a11_0932900.speaker: Evans
a11_0932900.text: 11, Houston. Looks like the Command Module's been in good shape. Black Team has been watching it real closely for you.

a11_0932900.speaker: Collins
a11_0932900.text: We sure appreciate that. [Pause.] Cos I sure haven't.

a11_0932900.speaker: Collins
a11_0932900.text: I say: Because I sure have not.

a11_0932900.speaker: Evans
a11_0932900.text: Apollo 11. Thirty seconds. AOS will be 94 plus 21.

a11_0932900.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0932900.text: This is Apollo Control. We have had Loss Of Signal from Apollo 11 as it went over the hill. Now tracking through the Madrid station during this series of revolutions. Next acquisition, as Apollo 11 comes back around the east limb of the Moon on the next revolution, will be at 94 hours, 21 minutes Ground Elapsed Time; some 43 minutes from now. And at 93 hours, 36 minutes Ground Elapsed Time; this is Apollo Control.

a11_0942100.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0942100.text: After having breakfast and getting all squared away after the night's rest period, the crew will have a rather busy day today including the first manned landing on the Moon. Some of the preliminary times being generated now for maneuvers of the day will include separation at - a separation burn at 100 hours, 39 minutes, 50 seconds. Here goes the call.

a11_0942100.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0942100.text: Roger. How do you read the Biomed in the LMP with the LCG on? Over.

a11_0942100.speaker: Evans
a11_0942100.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We have good data on all three crewmen. No. Belay that. The Commander we do not have yet.

a11_0942100.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0942100.text: Roger. He's not up just yet.

a11_0945000.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0945000.text: Houston, Apollo 11. We just had a very good view of the landing site. We can pick out most all of the features we've identified previously.

a11_0945000.speaker: Evans
a11_0945000.text: 11, Houston. Roger. Sounds real fine. And, 11, I have your maneuver PAD and consumables update whenever you want them. [Long pause.]

a11_0945000.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0945000.text: Stand by a little, please.

a11_0945000.speaker: Evans
a11_0945000.text: Roger. We're standing by. And that's the block data on the maneuver PAD, by the way.

a11_0945000.speaker: Collins
a11_0945000.text: Houston, Apollo 11 is a couple of minutes away from this rolling right 40 degrees to roll 122, pitch 229, yaw 0. Over.

a11_0945000.speaker: Evans
a11_0945000.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Roger. We're standing by.

a11_0945000.speaker: Collins
a11_0945000.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Ready to copy.

a11_0945000.speaker: Evans
a11_0945000.text: Roger. Apollo 11, Houston. Here's your block data, TEI-30. Over.

a11_0945000.speaker: Collins
a11_0945000.text: Ready to copy.

a11_0945000.speaker: Evans
a11_0945000.text: SPS/G&N: 36639; your Noun 48, minus 0.72, plus 0.51; your Noun 33, 135:24:40.00; Noun 81, plus 3217.8, plus 0603.6, minus 0130.4; your pitch, 064. The rest is NA. Ullage; two jet, 16 seconds. And it's based on LOI REFSMMAT. Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0945000.speaker: Collins
a11_0945000.text: Roger. TEI-30, SPS/G&N: 36639; minus 0.72, plus 0.51; 135:24:40.00; plus 3217.8, plus 0603.6, minus 0130.4; pitch 064. Two jets, 16 seconds. LOI REFSMMAT. Over.

a11_0945000.speaker: Evans
a11_0945000.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Readback correct. Your consumables update? [Long pause.]

a11_0945000.speaker: Collins
a11_0945000.text: Yeah. Go ahead.

a11_0945000.speaker: Evans
a11_0945000.text: Roger. GET 91 plus 30, minus 7 percent; Alpha, minus 8; Bravo, minus 2.5; Charlie, minus 10; Delta, minus 6.5. H 2 total, minus 2 pounds. Oxygen total, plus 9 pounds. Over.

a11_0945000.speaker: Collins
a11_0945000.text: Okay. Thank you. And on board, we're reading for Quad Alpha, 75 percent; Bravo, 78; Charlie, 78; and Delta, 77 percent.

a11_0945000.speaker: Evans
a11_0945000.text: 11, Houston. We copy. [Pause.]

a11_0945000.speaker: Evans
a11_0945000.text: Apollo 11, Houston. I have your baseline altitude update now, if Buzz is ready to copy.

a11_0945000.speaker: Collins
a11_0945000.text: Go ahead.

a11_0945000.speaker: Evans
a11_0945000.text: Roger. Alpha 1 is 500, that's 500 feet above the landing site. Over.

a11_0945000.speaker: Collins
a11_0945000.text: Okay. Alpha 1 is 500 feet above the landing site. Thank you. [Long pause.]

a11_0945000.speaker: Collins
a11_0945000.text: Houston, Apollo 11. Our crew status report for sleep: CDR, 5.5; CMP, 6.0; LMP, 5.0. Over.

a11_0945000.speaker: Evans
a11_0945000.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Roger. We have that now.

a11_0945000.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0945000.text: This is Apollo Control. Still up live with the air-ground circuit on the tenth revolution around the Moon. Crew reported that the Commander had 5½ hours of sleep during the night; Command Module Pilot, 6 hours; Lunar Module Pilot, 5 hours. Now 95 hours and 5 minutes into the mission. Another 27 minutes remaining in this pass 'til Loss Of Signal. Continuing to monitor air-ground circuit. We'll leave it up live until Loss Of Signal.

a11_0951609.speaker: Evans
a11_0951609.text: Roger. The Black Bugle just arrived with some morning news briefs if you're ready.

a11_0951609.speaker: Evans
a11_0951609.text: Okay. Church services around the world today are mentioning Apollo 11 in their prayers. President Nixon's worship service at the White House is also dedicated to the mission, and our fellow astronaut, Frank Borman, is still in there pitching and will read the passage from Genesis which was read on Apollo 8 last Christmas. The Cabinet and members of Congress, with emphasis on the Senate and House Space Committees, have been invited, along with a number of other guests. Buzz, your son, Andy, got a tour of MSC yesterday. Your Uncle Bob Moon accompanied him on the visit which included the LRL. Amo

a11_0951609.speaker: Evans
a11_0951609.text: Roger. Among the large headlines concerning Apollo this morning, is one asking that you watch for a lovely girl with a big rabbit. An ancient legend says a beautiful Chinese girl called Chang-O has been living there for 4,000 years. It seems she was banished to the Moon because she stole the pill of immortality from her husband. You might also look for her companion, a large Chinese rabbit, who is easy to spot since he is always standing on his hind feet in the shade of a cinnamon tree. The name of the rabbit is not reported.

a11_0951609.speaker: Collins
a11_0951609.text: Okay. We'll keep a close eye out for the bunny girl.

a11_0951609.speaker: Evans
a11_0951609.text: Roger. You residents of the spacecraft Columbia may be interested in knowing that today is Independence Day in the country of Colombia. [Pause.] Gloria Diaz of the Philippines was crowned Miss Universe last night. She defeated 60 other girls for the global beauty title. Miss Diaz is 18, with black hair and eyes, and measures 34½, 23, 34½. First runner-up was Miss Australia, followed by Miss Israel, and Miss Japan. [Pause.] While you're on your way back Tuesday night, the American and National League Allstars will be playing ball in Washington. Mel Stottlemyre of the Yankees is ex

a11_0951609.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0951609.text: Thanks very much. We appreciate the news. [Long pause.]

a11_0951609.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0951609.text: Black Team, we'll be looking for an interesting day with you all tomorrow.

a11_0951609.speaker: Evans
a11_0951609.text: Roger. We'll be going off here shortly, and we'll pick you up in the morning for sure.

a11_0951609.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0951609.text: This is Apollo Control. Some 9 minutes, 27 seconds remaining until Loss Of Signal on this tenth revolution in lunar orbit. Crew preparing, now that they've finished breakfast and gotten a lot of their other items out of the way such as their crew checklist, sleep status and so on, preparing for manning the LM for the second time and preparing for the day's activities which will culminate in landing this afternoon. Apollo 11 is presently in an orbit with a pericynthion of 55.7 nautical miles [103.2 km]; apocynthion, 63.8 nautical miles [118.2 km]. Lunar orbit velocity; 5,368 feet per second [1,

a11_0953015.speaker: Evans
a11_0953015.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Three minutes to LOS. AOS at 96 plus 20.

a11_0953015.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0953015.text: This is Apollo Control. We have apparently had Loss Of Signal from the spacecraft. Here in Mission Control, we're in the process of changing shifts. Flight Director Gene Kranz and the White Team of flight controllers coming on to replace Flight Director Glynn Lunney. The Capsule Communicator on this shift will be Astronaut Charlie Duke. We'll reacquire the spacecraft again in a little over 45 minutes, coming up on the 11th revolution of the Moon. At 95 hours, 34 minutes; this is Apollo Control.

a11_0953300.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0953300.text: Let's see, these things come in the Command Module don't they, those umbilicals?

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Neil, do you recall the highest rate you saw during this recent thruster activity? Did you say 0.4 or thereabouts?

a11_0961900.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0961900.text: What?

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Do you recall the - any kind of body rates that you saw during that thruster activity? Didn't you say something about 0.4? Maybe - remember when the SCS was acting up?

a11_0961900.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0961900.text: Ah...

a11_0961900.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0961900.text: Network says we have acquired signal. We'll stand by for the call to the crew.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Hello, Columbia. Houston. Do you read? Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Hello, Houston, this is Eagle. How do you read? Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Eagle, this is Houston. Are you calling? Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Roger. How do you read? Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger. Reading you about three-by, Buzz. A lot of noise on the loop. We think it's coming from Columbia, but we can't tell. We're unable to raise voice with him. Would he please go to High Gain. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Okay. I'll have him go to High Gain. It's probably the glycol pump you hear in the background, and I'm up to the point where I turn on the IMU. Would you recommend I hold off here for a few minutes or go ahead and power up the IMU? Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger. Stand by.

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Hey, get your High Gain working.

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Houston [garble]. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Houston, Columbia. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Eagle, this is Houston. You can turn on the IMU. Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Roger. Understand [garble].

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Houston, this is Columbia. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Columbia, this is Houston. Do you read? Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Houston, Columbia. Reading you loud and clear. How me? Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Hey, Buzz? How about...

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Hello, Eagle. This is Houston. We've got a noisy downlink on the down-voice backup. Would you please select S-band Voice to Voice? Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Columbia, this is Houston. Do you read? Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Houston, Columbia. Reading you loud and clear. How me?

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Rog. You're about three-by, Mike. We got a lot of noise in the background. It's clearing up now. Break. Eagle, Houston. Do you read? Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Houston, Eagle. About four-by-four. Go ahead.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger. Just getting a voice check. Say the page you're on in the activation checklist. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Roger. I'm on page 27. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger. Understand 27. We copy. Out. [Long pause.]

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Columbia, this is Houston. Would you please give us P00 and Accept. We have a state vector for you. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Stand by one.

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Houston, Columbia. You have P00 and Accept, and how are you reading me now?

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger. Understand, we have P00 and Accept. You're about three-by in - on the voice, Mike. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Okay. You're coming in loud and clear, and I'm configured for normal voice. If you've got any switch changes, you wanna let me know?

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Rog. We've got some noise somewhere in the system down here, I think. We're working on it. And I've got a 130 landmark update for you, and also a DAP load whenever you're ready to copy. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Stand by one. [Long pause.]

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Go ahead with the 130 update.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger, Mike. Coming at you with the 130. T1 is 98:37:35; T2, 98:42:44, 4 miles north. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Okay. T1, 98:37:35; T2, 98:42:44; 4 miles north of track. And go ahead with your DAP load.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger. CSM weight, 36651; LM weight, 33627; pitch trim, minus 0.72; yaw trim, plus 0.51. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Both are good readbacks. Out.

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Houston, Eagle. Are you satisfied with the LGC self test? Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger. Understand. You passed the LGC self test. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Negative. I was asking you if you were satisfied with it. As far as I can tell, it's satisfactory. And also the primary Evap flow is actuated to number 1 at 96:05. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger. Copy on the primary Evap. We've got the low bit rate, Buzz. We couldn't see that LGC self test. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a11_0961900.speaker: Collins
a11_0961900.text: Houston, Columbia. The docking tunnel index angle remains unchanged.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger. Copy. Out. [Long pause.]

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Houston, Eagle is going to secondary transmitter/receiver and secondary power amplifier, and I'll check with you in 60 seconds. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger. Stand by. We're standing by. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Columbia, Houston. We are through with the computer. You can go back to Block. Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Houston, Eagle. On secondary transmitter/receiver and power amplifier, how do you read? Over. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Rog. Reading you five-by, Buzz. How me? 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. Out.

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Rog. About - That's the same as before. Switching back to Primary.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Houston, Eagle. Back on Primary, and I'm ready to proceed with the steerable antenna activation.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger. We're standing by, Buzz. Go ahead. Over. [Pause.]

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: And I'll go to Biomed left - ah, right momentarily.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger.

a11_0961900.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0961900.text: LM communications engineer reports that we're on the LM steerable antenna, which apparently accounts for the quiet communications we're getting at this point.

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Houston, Eagle. Got a very nice lock-on - lock-on on the steerable antenna, and you should be receiving Biomed right and PCM high. Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Rog, Eagle. We got you five-by. It's really beautiful. We've got the high bit rate and the Biomed. Out. [Pause.]

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Eagle, Houston. Do you copy? Over.

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Roger. Copy.

a11_0961900.speaker: MCC speaker
a11_0961900.text: You got CMP on [unclear, may be IRIG] 5 and LMP on [unclear, may be IRIG] 7.

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: Houston, Eagle. For your information, we're doing the glycol pump check now.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger. Copy. [Long pause.]

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: And there's the secondary glycol pump.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a11_0961900.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0961900.text: And I'm on secondary, or number 2 pump right now, and I'll hold here for a couple of seconds and then switch back to number 1.

a11_0961900.speaker: Duke
a11_0961900.text: Roger.

a11_0964247.speaker: Duke
a11_0964247.text: Ap - Columbia, Houston. Over.

a11_0964247.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0964247.text: Houston.

a11_0964247.speaker: Collins/Aldrin
a11_0964247.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a11_0964247.speaker: Duke
a11_0964247.text: Roger, Columbia. We noticed the DAP configuration. We'd like you to turn off B3 and C4, Mike, and for register 2 in the DAP, we'd like all ones. Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0964247.speaker: Collins
a11_0964247.text: B3 and C4 are both O-F-F on panel 8, and I understand you want - Say again what you want on register 2.

a11_0964247.speaker: Duke
a11_0964247.text: Roger. In the DAP, we'd like you to load all ones. Over.

a11_0964247.speaker: Collins
a11_0964247.text: Alright. [Long pause.]

a11_0964247.speaker: Duke
a11_0964247.text: Columbia, Houston. Did you hit the Command Reset around - after LOS on the last pass? Over.

a11_0964247.speaker: Collins
a11_0964247.text: That's affirmative. When we were having difficulty getting you, Charlie, I pushed the Command Reset to make sure I had control of High Gain.

a11_0964247.speaker: Duke
a11_0964247.text: Roger. Thank you much. We're in good shape now. Over.

a11_0964247.speaker: Collins
a11_0964247.text: Okay.

a11_0964247.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0964247.text: Houston, Eagle. Can you tell me if you're picking up Biomed on the CDR now? Over.

a11_0964247.speaker: Duke
a11_0964247.text: Stand by. [Long pause.]

a11_0964247.speaker: Duke
a11_0964247.text: Eagle, Houston. We're not getting any Biomed from the CDR now. Over.

a11_0964247.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0964247.text: Roger. Understand.

a11_0964247.speaker: Duke
a11_0964247.text: Eagle, Houston. We got the Biomed on the Commander now. Over. [Pause.]

a11_0964247.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0964247.text: Very good. Thank you.

a11_0964247.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0964247.text: Houston, Eagle. We're ready for an E-memory dump if you are. Over.

a11_0964247.speaker: Duke
a11_0964247.text: Roger. We're ready. Go. [Long pause.]

a11_0964247.speaker: Duke
a11_0964247.text: Eagle, this is Houston. We see the optics zero switch on. Before you take some marks, don't forget to cycle it back off and on, and then on. Over.

a11_0964247.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0964247.text: Rog. Houston, Eagle here. I wish we had one of those optics. I'll tell Mike about it.

a11_0964247.speaker: Duke
a11_0964247.text: Roger, Columbia. Excuse me. Sorry about that.

a11_0964247.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0964247.text: This is Apollo Control. Armstrong is now in the Lunar Module, in Eagle, and the LM activation and check-out appears to be going along very well, somewhat ahead of schedule.

a11_0965704.speaker: Duke
a11_0965704.text: Eagle, Houston. Could you give us a hack on the time that you switched to LM power and also verify that we're on Glycol Pump 1. Over. [Pause.]

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: This is Eagle. We're on Pump 1, stand by for the switch-over time.

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: The switch time to LM power is 95:54:00. Over.

a11_0965704.speaker: Duke
a11_0965704.text: Roger. Copy, Neil. Is Buzz back in the Columbia now? Over.

a11_0965704.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0965704.text: This is Apollo Control. We have about 33 minutes left in this pass before Loss Of Signal. Neil Armstrong confirmed that the LM power switch occurred at 95 hours, 54 minutes; which would have put the - put that activity about 30 minutes ahead of the Flight Plan's schedule, and that appears to be about the pace that the crew is holding - that Armstrong and Aldrin are holding, and getting the LM activated and checked out. At this time, Buzz Aldrin has returned to the Command and Service Module where he'll be donning his pressure garment and then re-join Armstrong in Eagle.

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: Hello, Columbia, this is Eagle on Simplex B. How do you read?

a11_0965704.speaker: Collins
a11_0965704.text: You're loud and clear in Simplex B, Neil.

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: Roger. Read you loud and clear. [Pause.]

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: Okay. Would you configure for Simplex A, please?

a11_0965704.speaker: Collins
a11_0965704.text: Roger. Going to Simplex A. [Long pause.]

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: Columbia, Eagle. How do you read on VHF-A?

a11_0965704.speaker: Collins
a11_0965704.text: Reading you loud and clear on A.

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: Roger. Read you loud and clear. [Pause.]

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: And I'm ready to get a time hack from you. Load the CSM time.

a11_0965704.speaker: Collins
a11_0965704.text: Do you want the T Ephem first?

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: Let's get your clock first and then we'll get T Ephem .

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: Give me a time to load.

a11_0965704.speaker: Collins
a11_0965704.text: 97:01:30. Correction on that, Neil. 97 - make that 97:03:30. [Long pause.]

a11_0965704.speaker: Collins
a11_0965704.text: Okay. And you've got about a minute to go.

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: Okay. Let's do a 06 65 on my Mark. [Pause.]

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: Okay. I'm within three-hundredths. That's within our ability to keep together, I think.

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: Okay. Now you want to give me T Ephem Verb 05, Noun 01, Enter?

a11_0965704.speaker: Collins
a11_0965704.text: Okay. I've got Verb 05, Noun 01, Enter. Going to 17 06, Enter.

a11_0965704.speaker: Collins
a11_0965704.text: And I'm standing by configured to record your PCM data. [Long pause.]

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: And I'm ready to start on a docked IMU coarse align when you are. And when you're ready, go Min Deadband, Att Hold.

a11_0965704.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0965704.text: Okay. Now I need your Noun 20. [Pause.]

a11_0965704.speaker: Collins
a11_0965704.text: Okay. I got Verb 06, Noun 20. Give me a Mark on it.

a11_0971134.speaker: Duke
a11_0971134.text: Eagle, Houston. That coarse align looked good to us. Over.

a11_0971134.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0971134.text: Okay, Mike. Your Attitude Hold's no longer required.

a11_0971134.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0971134.text: Okay, Mike. I'd like to copy a Noun 20 again, [Verb] 06, Noun 20. Be on my Mark.

a11_0971134.speaker: Collins
a11_0971134.text: Okay, I read plus 11154, plus 20792, plus 00230. Over.

a11_0971134.speaker: Duke
a11_0971134.text: Eagle, Houston. We have the angles. I'll read 'em back. Over. For the Command Module; 11154, 20792, 00230. For the LM; 18995, 02852, 35863. Over.

a11_0971134.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0971134.text: That's correct for Eagle and Command Module.

a11_0971134.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0971134.text: Did you get the time? Was 97:14:20.

a11_0971134.speaker: Duke
a11_0971134.text: Columbia and Eagle - LOS for both spacecraft, 97:32; AOS, 98:18. Houston, out.

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Eagle, Houston. We have your gyro torquing angles if you're ready to copy. Over. [Pause.]

a11_0972135.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0972135.text: Roger. We're ready to copy.

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Roger. Eagle. For X, minus 00060; Y, plus 00620; Z, plus 01080. Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0972135.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0972135.text: Understand. X, minus 00060; Y, plus 00620; Z, plus 01080.

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Roger, Eagle. Good read-back. Out.

a11_0972135.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0972135.text: Houston, this is Eagle. Do you want us to go ahead and do a Verb 42 at this time?

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Stand by. That's affirmative, Eagle. We'd like you to go ahead and fine align. Over.

a11_0972135.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0972135.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a11_0972135.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0972135.text: Houston, Eagle, LMP. How do you read? Over.

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Rog. Five-by, Buzz. How me? Over.

a11_0972135.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0972135.text: Oh, loud and clear. I'm going to be going through an ascent battery check. You want to check my Biomed briefly? Over.

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Roger. Go ahead. [Long pause.]

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Eagle, Houston. We got a good Biomed on you, Buzz. Over.

a11_0972135.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0972135.text: Okay. Let me know where it ought to be at this point.

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Roger. You can stay there at that point. When we go LOS, we'd like you to go Off on the Biomed. Over.

a11_0972135.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0972135.text: Roger. [Long pause.]

a11_0972135.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0972135.text: Do you copy those angles, Houston. Torquing angles?

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Roger. They're correct. You can torque. Over.

a11_0972135.speaker: Collins
a11_0972135.text: Okay.

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We have about 4 minutes to LOS. Next AOS 98:18. Over.

a11_0972135.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0972135.text: Eagle. Roger.

a11_0972135.speaker: Collins
a11_0972135.text: Columbia. Roger. [Long pause.]

a11_0972135.speaker: Collins
a11_0972135.text: Eagle, Columbia. [Pause.]

a11_0972135.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0972135.text: Columbia, Eagle. Go ahead.

a11_0972135.speaker: Collins
a11_0972135.text: Roger. The capture latches in the probe, are engaged in the drogue. Would you like to check them from your side?

a11_0972135.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0972135.text: Rog. Stand by. [Pause.]

a11_0972135.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0972135.text: Houston, Eagle. ED Battery A is 37.0 and Battery B is 36.9. Over.

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Roger. Copy both of those, Buzz. Out. [Long pause.]

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Eagle, Houston. We looked at the E-Memory. It's Go. Over.

a11_0972135.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0972135.text: Roger. E-Memory Go. [Long pause.]

a11_0972135.speaker: Armstrong
a11_0972135.text: Mike, the capture latches look good.

a11_0972135.speaker: Collins
a11_0972135.text: Thank you. [Pause.]

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Eagle, Houston. We'd like you to go to the Omni antenna, and next AOS, we'd like you to be in forward. Over.

a11_0972135.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0972135.text: Roger. Going to - Which Omni do you want now, aft? [Long pause.]

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Eagle, Houston. We'd like aft now and forward at AOS. Over.

a11_0972135.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0972135.text: Roger.

a11_0972135.speaker: Duke
a11_0972135.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Thirty seconds to LOS. Both spacecraft looking good going over the hill. Out.

a11_0972135.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0972135.text: This is Apollo Control. We've had Loss Of Signal now. We'll next acquire the spacecraft in about 46 minutes at a Ground Elapsed Time of 98 hours, 18 minutes. During that pass, Armstrong and Aldrin in the Lunar Module began checking out, activating the Lunar Module, and they appeared to finish about 30 minutes ahead of the scheduled time in the Flight Plan. They began early and maintained the pace. Both spacecraft looking very good at this time and everything progressing very smoothly. On the next revolution, revolution 12, the crew will continue activation and checkout of Lunar Module systems.

a11_0981600.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0981600.text: We're now about 15 seconds from re-acquisition of Apollo 11. Spacecraft currently in an orbit with an apocynthion of 63½ nautical miles [117.6 km], a pericynthion of 55.9 [103.5 km]. As we're continuing to see the apocynthion drop and pericynthion raise, as the orbit becomes more and more circular.

a11_0981600.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0981600.text: We should have Acquisition Of Signal shortly. We will have some noise on the circuits until the LM steerable and the CSM High Gain antennas are brought into play.

a11_0981600.speaker: Mission Control
a11_0981600.text: CapCom Charlie Duke putting in a call to the crew. We'll continue to stand by.

a11_0981600.speaker: Duke
a11_0981600.text: Apollo 11, Houston. We're standing by. Over. [No answer.]

a11_0981600.speaker: Duke
a11_0981600.text: Columbia, Houston. Do you read? Over. [No answer.]

a11_0981600.speaker: Duke
a11_0981600.text: Eagle, Houston. Do you read? Over. [No answer.]

a11_0981600.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0981600.text: Yeah, I'm working on the High Gain right now.

a11_0981600.speaker: Collins
a11_0981600.text: Okay, I'm reading him loud and clear.

a11_0981600.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0981600.text: You in the right attitude, Mike?

a11_0981600.speaker: Collins
a11_0981600.text: Houston, Columbia. You're loud and clear.

a11_0981600.speaker: Duke
a11_0981600.text: Eagle, Houston. No voice. Will you verify forward Omni? Over. [No answer.]

a11_0982500.speaker: Aldrin
a11_0982500.text: Roger. Understand.

a11_0982500.speaker: Collins
a11_0982500.text: Houston, Columbia.

a11_0982500.speaker: Duke
a11_0982500.text: Eagle, Houston. Would you select S-Band Voice to Voice. Over. [Long pause.]

a11_0982500.speaker: Collins
a11_0982500.text: [Inaudible on air-ground] Roger. S-Band Voice to Voice. How do you read now?

a11_0982500.speaker: Collins
a11_0982500.text: Houston, Columbia. Over.

a11_0982500.speaker: Collins
a11_0982500.text: Houston, Columbia in Down Voice Backup. Do you read?

a11_0982500.speaker: Duke
a11_0982500.text: Roger. We read you. Columbia, did you call? Over.

a11_0982500.speaker: Collins
a11_0982500.text: Affirmative. Calling you in Down Voice Backup. How do you read me?

a11_0982500.speaker: Duke
a11_0982500.text: Rog. Better, Mike. We're reading you now about four-by. No voice at all with you earlier. Let's stay in this configuration. Eagle, are you in Voice mode? Over.

a11_0982500.speaker: Aldrin
