a11a1080053-1082505.text: (Garbled) We'll put my (PLSS) antenna up. (Pause)

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Okay.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Okay; how do you read now?

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Okay.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Okay. I think that's going to be better. (Pause) You read me all right now?

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Yeah.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Okay. That sounds pretty good. I guess it's a combination of the volume and the antenna. May have been just the volume that was way up too high. Why don't you try stowing it again; see if that makes any (difference). (Pause)

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Okay.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: All right. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1. That sounds pretty good.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: That's okay. [They are in the middle of Sur-31 . Each of them has a foot-long flat-wire antenna on the top of the backpack. When not in use, it is held down by a loop of fabric velcroed to the top surface of the OPS. Nominally, in the interest of not breaking it off as they move around inside the LM and crawl through the hatch, they would leave the antenna lying flat until they were outside; but, as here, if comm is poor, the checklist suggests raising the antenna.]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Better keep it (the microphone) pretty close to your mouth, though. Okay. (Reading from the checklist) Open up your audio circuit breaker, and disconnect the LM Comm cable. (Long Pause) [Houston has re-acquired Columbia as it came into view around the eastern limb of the Moon.]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Columbia, Columbia, this is Houston. Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Collins
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Houston, Columbia on the high gain. How do you read?

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Roger, Columbia. Reading you loud and clear on the high gain. We have enabled the one-way MSFN relay that you requested. The crew of Tranquility Base is currently donning PLSSs. The LMP has his PLSS on, Comm checks out, and the CDR is checking his Comm out now. Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Collins
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Sounds good. Thank you kindly. (Long Pause)

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Collins
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Houston, Columbia. I tweaked the (inertial) platform up on the back side. I have a P52 option 3 when you're ready to copy the data.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Go ahead, Columbia.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Collins
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Roger. Stars 43 and 44: star angle difference four balls one, Noun 93 plus 000...

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Audio circuit breaker Closed.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: All right, on your panel, VHF A, Off; VHF B, Off.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: All right, RCU PTT to Main.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Columbia, this is Houston. Copy star angle difference of 4 balls 1; Noun 93, plus 00057...

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: PLSS mode switch to B.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Got a warning tone?

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: ...time of 107:30:38. Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Collins
a11a1080053-1082505.text: You got it.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Roger. ...

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: (Garbled under Bruce).

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: ...Are you reading Tranquility Base now?

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Okay. You've got an O and a P. [These warning flags are on the top of the Remote Control Unit ( RCU ) and indicate that there is no oxygen flow and that the suit isn't pressurized. At this point in the EVA preps, Neil and Buzz are merely checking to see that the warning system is working properly.]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: What is your O 2 quantity, by the way?

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: O 2 quantity is about 91 (percent).

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: I've got 92.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Okay. Now I'm going to Mode Select B. (Long Pause) Warning tone. (Pause) That where you want to be?

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: I'm in B.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: (Garbled) A.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Going to A. I'm in A.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Okay. How do you read me?

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: I read you.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: You're loud and clear.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: I got another warning tone. (Pause) (Garbled)

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Out now? Okay? [They have just finished Sur-31 .]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Both. PLSS mode select AR.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: AR. How do you read?

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Didn't get a warning tone.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: I got one.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Got it? (Pause) Okay, warning tone is out. Verify PLSS O 2 bottle pressure greater than 85.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: It is.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Do you have voice with "each other".

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Yup.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Houston, Tranquility. How do you read? Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Neil. Neil. This is Houston through Tranquility. Radio check. Over. [Now that they are on PLSS comm , the path is from Houston through the LM to the PLSS antennas, then back through the LM EVA antenna (which they raised earlier) and on to Houston.]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Roger. Houston, this is Neil. How do you read?

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Neil, this is Houston. We're reading you loud and clear. Break, break. Buzz, this is Houston through Tranquility. Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Roger, Houston. This is Buzz through Tranquility. How do you read? Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: We're reading you loud and clear, Buzz. Out. (Pause)

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: And you're getting a signal on the TV? Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: (Making a mis-identification) That's affirmative, Neil. The data that we're receiving looks good and we are receiving Sync pulses and a black signal on TV. [At the top of Sur-30 , they closed the TV circuit breaker so that Houston could make sure that they were getting a good signal. The TV is inside the MESA (Modular Equipment Stowage Assembly) which is folded up against the side of the LM just to the north of the ladder. In addition to the TV, the MESA contains the rock boxes and various tools. Once he crawls backwards out of the hatch, Neil will reach to his left and, by pulling on a lanyar

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Okay. You'll find that the area around the ladder is in a complete dark shadow, so we're going to have some problem with TV, but I'm sure you'll get a picture from the lighted horizon (garbled).

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: This is Houston. We copy, and right toward the end of your transmission after you mentioned "lighted horizon", you trailed off down into the noise level, Neil. Over. [Comm Break]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Columbia, this is Houston. Are you reading Tranquility all right on the relay? Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Collins
a11a1080053-1082505.text: I believe so. I haven't heard anything from him lately, and it's breaking up. But up until about 3 minutes ago, I was reading them loud and clear.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Roger. Sounds like you're getting it all.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Collins
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Thank you. [Comm Break]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Tranquility Base, this is Houston. We request you open the TV circuit breaker at the present time. We've had it on about 15 minutes now with the MESA closed. Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Roger. (Garbled) (Long Pause) [Now that Houston is getting a good signal from the TV, they want to turn it off so that it doesn't overheat in the well-insulated confines of the MESA. They will turn it on again when Neil is ready to go out. Evidently, Neil and Buzz overlooked that step on Sur-32 and Bruce is reminding them, without calling attention to the mistake.]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Houston, do you read (garbled)

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Say again, Neil.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: (Garbled) (Pause)

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Neil. Neil. This is Houston. I can hear you trying to transmit; however, your transmission is breaking up. Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: (Garbled)

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Buzz. Buzz. This is Houston. Do you read? Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Roger, Houston. This is Buzz. How do you read? Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Roger. You're coming through loud and clear, Buzz. It's a beautiful signal.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Neil's got his antenna up now. Let's see if he comes through any better now.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Okay. Houston, this is Neil. How do you read?

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Neil, this is Houston. Reading you beautifully. (Long Pause)

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: (Static) My antenna's scratching the roof.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: We copy (that) your antenna (is) scratching the roof. Roger. [Aldrin, from the 1969 Technical Debrief - "The initial comm checkout on the audio panel and the various communications checks that we made in the FM mode all seemed to go quite well, until we started switching the PLSS modes. For a while, we ascribed some of the difficulty perhaps to the antenna being stowed. So we unstowed Neil's, and that didn't help immediately. A little later, it seemed to help out, but then we got back into about the same problem, so I stowed his antenna. There didn't seem to be any particular rhyme or reason t

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Do we have a Go for cabin depress? (Pause; no answer) [In the interest of caution, the Flight Director is making a final check of all systems before giving the Go. Neil and Buzz are starting the paragraph "Final Systems Prep for Egress" on page Sur-32 . They have attached their OPS oxygen hoses to the PLSSs and the OPS actuator cables to the RCUs. Training photo S69-32234 shows Buzz's OPS actuator on the left side of his RCU mockup.]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: They hear everything but that. Houston, this is Tranquility. We're standing by for a Go for cabin depress. Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Tranquility Base, this is Houston. You are Go for cabin depressurization. Go for cabin depressurization.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Roger. Thank you. [I, for one, remember getting excited at this point in the proceedings, thinking that they were close to opening the hatch. In reality, they still have to configure the LM ECS (Environmental Control System) for the depress, get their helmets on, get themselves off of LM oxygen, cooling water, and comm, hook themselves up to the PLSSs, and get their gloves on. It will be another half hour before they start the depress.]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Okay, Descent Water Valve is Closed.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Okay.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Verify Cabin Fan Number 1 circuit breaker open.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: (Garbled) [Neil is turning off the fan which circulates oxygen through the ECS. He and Buzz will be able to hear the fan stop running but soon will also note two caution lights, again as a test of the caution-and-warning system.]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Suit Fan number 1 breaker. We'll have to pull that one out. (Garbled) (Pause) Now wait a minute.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Columbia, this is Houston. Your LM line-of-sight Comm acquisition with the Tranquility Base is 108 plus 29. LOS is plus 42. Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Suit Circuit Relief Valve to Auto.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: In Auto. [The LM ECS is controlled with a combination of circuit breakers located on the panel at Buzz's right shoulder and by various valves located on the ECS cabinet located behind Buzz's station. Some of the valves are located on the forward surface and some on the inboard surface. With both of them wearing PLSSs and their freedom of motion restricted, it is Neil who operates most of the ECS valves, reaching across with his right hand.] [Armstrong - "It was easier for me to see the controls and to reach them."]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Suit Gas...

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Collins
a11a1080053-1082505.text: I'm going over to (garbled) I'll pick you up...

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: ...Diverter Valve to Egress. Pull. [With the Suit Gas Diverter Valve in Egress, they are cutting off the flow of oxygen from the ECS to the cabin. The Diverter Valve has a push/pull control.]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Collins
a11a1080053-1082505.text: ...on Omni C or D.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: (To Mike) Stand by please.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Verify Master Alarm. Pushbutton Light, Reset. (Pause) ECS Caution Light and Water Separator Caution Light (will come) On.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Takes a while for the water separator. Maybe.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: I don't understand. Suit Fan Number 1 circuit breaker, Open. (Long Pause) [They are waiting for the caution-and-warning system to sense that the ECS fan and the airflow-driven water separator have stopped operating. This typically takes 4 minutes.]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: McCandless
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Buzz, this is Houston. We'd like you to pull the Suit Fan Delta-P circuit breaker on panel 16. Over.

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Roger, I have it. [Houston is reminding Buzz to turn off a sensor which detects a pressure difference across the fan, another indication of whether or not the fan is running. They had skipped over that step.]

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: That's what the difference... Yeah. (Pause)

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Cabin Gas (Return Valve , Egress).

a11a1080053-1082505.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1080053-1082505.text: Yep. (Pause) It's in Egress. (Long Pause) [They are verifying that there can be no flow from the cabin into the ECS.] Audio Clip from the Public Affairs loop starting at about 108:25:05. a11a1085327-1091548.text: Okay. "Verify the PGA pressure is above 4.5." Mine is 4.6.

a11a1085327-1091548.text: Okay. (Pause) [Sensors in the PLSSs have noted that, although the cabin pressure is low, the sublimators are not yet working. The sublimator consists of a sandwich of honeycomb plates on which, when exposed to vacuum, the feedwater turns to ice and it is the sublimation of the ice layer that provides cooling. The astronauts will not start the flow of feedwater until they get the hatch open and, by noting the warnings, they are making sure that the sensors are working.]

The filters will not be flown on subsequent missions. With the filter in place, cabin pressure drops from 5.0 pounds per square inch, absolute (psia) to 0.08 psia in 310 seconds versus 180 seconds without the filter. Use of both the forward and overhead valves without filters would bring the time down to 90 seconds. As soon as it broke the seal, it appeared as though I could see some small particles rushing out."] [Several of the crews noticed that ice crystals formed as the moist cabin air rushed out into the lunar vacuum. a11a1085327-1091548.text: Okay. Hold it from going closed and I'll get the valve to (Auto)...

a11a1124307-1132951.text: Rog; I'm copying.

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: McCandless
a11a1124307-1132951.text: Secondly, we will return to the nominal timeline with your scheduled wake-up of 121 hours and 12 minutes. We sort of slipped by lithium hydroxide canister change number 9 during the EVA and EVA Prep. We'd like you to accomplish that now. The Comm for sleep will be the normal lunar Comm configuration. (For) the RCS configuration, we're requesting you use quads Alpha and Bravo. A DAP data load for R2 should be 01111. Readback. Over.

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: Collins
a11a1124307-1132951.text: Roger. Oxygen fuel cell purge at 113:30. Return to the nominal timeline at 121 hours wake-up. Lithium hydroxide change number 9 right now. Normal lunar comm sleep configuration, I'm in that now. On the RCS, I understood before (that) you wanted to load the DAP register to 01100 which made sense on panel eight to pitch only on quad A, enable all on quad B, and C and D off. But you don't want to do that any more, huh? (No immediate answer) [Comm Break. The actual wake-up call will be at 120:59.]

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: McCandless
a11a1124307-1132951.text: Columbia; this is Houston. On your DAP load in R2, we're requesting a zero and four ones; that is 01111. Over.

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: Collins
a11a1124307-1132951.text: Okay. (Pause)

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: McCandless
a11a1124307-1132951.text: And you'll...

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: Collins
a11a1124307-1132951.text: Load's going in right now.

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: McCandless
a11a1124307-1132951.text: Roger. And you'll be enabling quads Alpha and Bravo on the Auto RCS select switches. Disable Charlie and Delta.

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: Collins
a11a1124307-1132951.text: All right. (Pause)

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: McCandless
a11a1124307-1132951.text: And we have a little less than 2 minutes to LOS. If you're still up, AOS next time around will be 114:04. Over.

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: Collins
a11a1124307-1132951.text: Roger. (Pause)

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: McCandless
a11a1124307-1132951.text: And, Columbia, if it's agreeable with you, we'd like you to stay awake until we have one successful re-acquisition on the high-gain antenna. And I guess you can plan on turning in shortly after AOS on this next pass. Over.

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: Collins
a11a1124307-1132951.text: Okay.

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: McCandless
a11a1124307-1132951.text: Roger. Out. (Long Pause) Tranquility Base. Tranquility Base. This is Houston. Radio check. Over.

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1124307-1132951.text: Go ahead. Houston.

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: McCandless
a11a1124307-1132951.text: Roger. Reading you loud and clear. Just wanted to make sure we still had Comm. 113:17:52 Armstrong: Roger. We just finished up...We're just finishing up our eat period. Be ready to go back into Prep for Depress.

a11a1124307-1132951.speaker: McCandless
a11a1124307-1132951.text: Roger. [Very Long Comm Break. The following audio sequences were accumulated during a press briefing.] MP3 Audio Clip (53 min 03 sec; 49 Mb) from the Public Affairs loop starting at about 113:46:23. Clip courtesy John Stoll, ACR Senior Technician at NASA Johnson.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Tranquility Base, this is Houston. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Go ahead, Houston.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. On your next depressurization, it's acceptable to use the overhead hatch dump valve in addition to or instead of the forward hatch dump valve to speed up the depressurization of the cabin. I have a T13 update for you. And if you could, sometime here, give us P00 and Data: we'll uplink you a new CSM state vector. Over. [The overhead valve has about twice the flow rate of the forward dump valve because it isn't equipped with a bacterial filter. However, they now have samples in the rock box so the filter is less important. The photograph of LTA-1 at the Cradle of Aviation Museum shows the

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: All right. (Pause)

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1134623-1145426.text: You've got the DSKY .

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Your T13 time (the planned lift-off) is 124:22:02. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. T13, 124:22...Is that 'zero two'? Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: That's affirmative. That is zero two. And do you have a time estimate for us until you're ready to start cabin Depress? Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Fifteen minutes, maybe?

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. [Comm Break] [Aldrin, from the 1969 Technical Debrief - "There's no getting around it, it's another EVA Prep exercise. It's easier (because they stay on LM systems rather than having to hook up the PLSSs), but you still have to go through the same exercises such as pressure-integrity check, bleeding the cabin down, and configuring the ECS (Environmental Control System). I guess if you have two EVAs, it probably would be nicer to jettison your equipment at the beginning of the second one, rather than (getting in after the first EVA, repressurizing, hooking up to the LM ECS and) having to

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Tranquility Base, this is Houston. Uplink complete. The computer's yours, and you can go out of Data.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. [Comm Break] [Former Mercury Astronaut Deke Slayton, the Director of Flight Crew Operations who has primary responsibility for crew selection, joins the conversation. Alan Shepard works for Slayton and is Head of the Astronaut Office.]

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Slayton
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Tranquility Base, Houston.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Go ahead. Tranquility Base, here.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Slayton
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Just want to let you guys know that, since you're an hour and a half over your timeline and we're all taking a day off tomorrow, we're going to leave you. See you later.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: I don't blame you a bit.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Slayton
a11a1134623-1145426.text: That's a real great day, guys. I really enjoyed it.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Thank you. You couldn't have enjoyed it as much as we did.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Slayton
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1134623-1145426.text: It was great.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Slayton
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Sure wish you'd hurry up and get that trash out of there, though.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Yes. We're just about to do it.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Slayton
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Okay. [Comm Break. The press briefing is over and normal taping of the mission audio resumes.]

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Tranquility Base, this is Houston. We show the suit relief valve still in the Auto position. It should be closed. Over. [Comm Break]

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Columbia, this is Houston. Over. (Long Pause)

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Collins
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Houston, Columbia. Go ahead.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. We've successfully re-acquired high-gain antenna. Unless you have some other traffic with us, I guess we'll bid you a good night and let you get some sleep, Mike. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Collins
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Okay. Sounds fine.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: And we're going to power down the voice subcarrier part of our uplink to you in order that we don't disturb you while we're talking to Tranquility Base. If you need us, just give us a call, and we can respond with a time lag of about a minute to a minute and a half in getting reconfigured. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Collins
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Okay. Thank you.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. And good night.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Collins
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Good night, Bruce. Thanks a lot. [Comm Break] [The LM crew starts depress procedures for the jettison at about 114:07, doing a suit integrity check at 3.5 psi.]

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Columbia, Columbia, this is Houston. We'd like you to Enable the thrusters in Bravo 1 and Bravo 2, Auto RCS Select. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Collins
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Okay. Bravo 1 and Bravo 2 Enable.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Out. (Long Pause; LM pressure starts toward zero) Tranquility, this is Houston. For a reference, which dump valve are you using? Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: We used the forward dump valve until about 2 psi, and we're using the overhead now.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Out.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: They're both open now. Restored Video Clip, PLSS Jettison 1 minutes 24 seconds ( 1.9 Mb FLV or 2.2 Mb MPEG ). May require VLC for playback. [Long Comm Break] [Because Neil and Buzz are both right-handed, it was probably Neil, standing on the left side of the cabin, who opened the overhead valve.] [The PLSS jettison comes at about 114:14. Both PLSSs could be seen on the TV as they tumbled out of the hatch, albeit not on the tape compilation available to us in 1991, which ends about about 112:24.] [ Ed von Renouard was a Video Tech at Honeysuckle Creek during Apollo and brought his Super-8 movie

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Houston, Tranquility Base. Repress complete. [Neil thinks they were on LM intercom, so they could talk to each other, and used the PTT trigger if they wanted to talk to Houston. Houston can monitor the proceedings through telemetry.]

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger, Tranquility. We observed your equipment jettison on the TV, and the passive seismic experiment recorded shocks when each PLSS hit the surface. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: (Joking) You can't get away with anything anymore, can you? 114:18:51 McCandless: No, indeed. [Comm Break] [Locally-produced signals such as the PLSS impacts provided insights into the depth of the regolith and its seismic properties.] [I asked about assignment to specialties after getting accepted into the Astronaut Corps.] [Armstrong - "It was true for a long period of time there that individuals got assigned to particular areas. Mine happened to be training and simulation. That was predominantly to make sure that crew interests were represented in all the meetings and discussions. So, if th

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Tranquility Base, this is Houston. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. When you get back into your surface checklist and come over to the Comm reconfiguration on page Surface-45, we'd like you to enable the ranging feature on your S-band. That is, when you come down to S-band configuration, instead of "Caution-and-Warning Electronics, Enable TV", we'd like you to go into the Range position and leave it there for as long as you conveniently can until you get ready to commence your rest period; and we'll try to get a little more ranging data on you. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Copy. [Houston is still trying to figure out exactly where they are.] [In the copy of Surface-45 in the ALSJ, the S-Band configuration line reads "S-BAND: PM, PRIM, PRIM, VOICE, PSM, CWEA ENABLE, LEFT, HI " where the last two items have been added by hand. The handprinted addition is quite tidy, suggesting that it was added pre-flight. These settings refer to the S-Band section of Panel 12 ( detail from Apollo 11 LM-5 "Eagle" poster by Mark Gray. Used with permission.) The first six items refer to the top row of switches: (1) Modulate switch to PM(FM); (2) XMTR/RCVR (Transmitter/Receive

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: And of course, when you get ready to turn in, go back into Caution-and-Warning, Enable and we'd like to say from all of us down here in Houston and really from all of us in all the countries in the entire world, we think that you've done a magnificent job up there today. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Thank you very much.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1134623-1145426.text: It's been a long day.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Yes, indeed. Get some rest there and have at it tomorrow. [Comm Break]

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Houston, Tranquility. Did you all come up with any other solution that we might try to the mission timer problem? Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Stand by, Tranquility. We'll be back with you in just a minute. (Long Pause) [Post-mission analysis indicated that the most likely cause of the timer failure was a cracked solder joint caused by differential thermal expansion within the unit. By the time Neil and Buzz turn it back on - in about 5 minutes - it will have been off for about 11 hours. The resulting cool down has reversed the differential expansion and, at least temporarily, has closed the solder crack. The timer will work properly during the rest of the mission. For subsequent missions, NASA subjected the units to longer periods o

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1134623-1145426.text: And, Houston, Tranquility. Have you had enough TV for today?

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Tranquility, this is Houston. Yes, indeed. It's been a mighty fine presentation there.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Okay. Signing off. See you again tomorrow.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. [Comm Break. They have turned the TV off to conserve power. Although there is plenty of power remaining in the batteries, there is no reason to continue powering the TV camera. The scene is not going to change prior to liftoff and, at the moment of staging, the circuit that provides power to the camera will be severed along with all other connections between the two LM stages.]

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Columbia. Columbia. This is Houston. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Collins
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Sorry to bother you, Columbia. Two things: we request that you select 10-degrees deadband in your DAP in accordance with the procedures on Foxtrot 9-7 in your checklist; and secondly, we'd like to leave a display on the DSKY that is not one that's cycling, being continuously updated. What you have when you get through widening the deadband will be a static display, and that'll be satisfactory. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Collins
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Okay.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Goodnight again. (Long Pause) Tranquility Base, this is Houston. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Go ahead.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. On your mission timer, we wanted to pull the circuit breaker and let it cool down for an hour and a half to 2 hours. I believe the breaker is currently open. It has been off, so go ahead and reset the mission timer circuit breaker. Put the timer control to Reset and hold it in Reset for three-zero (30) seconds, and then slew it to your desired settings left to right, and place the timer control to Start. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Okay. We'll try it. (Long Pause) [I asked about the need to get the timer working again, since they have at least one watch.] [Aldrin - "There are rapid-paced things that happen during the rendezvous and we like to have something that's a little easier to look at than an Omega ( watch )."]

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Houston, our mission timer seems to be slewing okay. You want to give us a time hack? Or can we get it off the CMC (Command Module Computer)...(correcting himself) LGC (Lunar Module Guidance Computer), I mean? (Pause) [Armstrong - "(Resetting the timer) was a matter of adjusting the numbers in the register to the current mission elapsed time and, then, on some kind of a mark from someplace, to engage the timer. It's not on (that is, driven by) any registers of the LGC; it's an independent unit."]

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger, Tranquility. I'll give you a time hack at 114:31:00. It's about 30 seconds from now. Over. (Long Pause) Stand by for a mark...

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Okay. (Garbled)

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: ...at 114:31. (Pause) Stand by. (Pause) Mark. (Pause) Tranquility, this is Houston. Did you copy my Mark at 114:31?

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Thank you, and our mission timer is running now.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Very good. And, I've got a consumables update for you if you're ready to copy or listen. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Stand by. (Pause) [I asked if they could hear any stuffiness in their voices, thinking of Jack Schmitt's allergic reaction to lunar dust.] [Aldrin - "It wasn't a very restful evening. How long have we been up?"] [They were awakened at 93:40 and, so, have been up for nearly 21 hours.] [Armstrong - "And temperature control was a bit of a problem for us and it could be that cabin temperature was contributing to something."] [I then told them about Jack Schmitt's apparent allergic reaction to lunar dust after the first Apollo 17 EVA - but not after the later ones.] [Armstrong - "I can't say that I

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Okay. Go ahead (with the consumables update). [Colin Mackellar has provided the following audio clip, recorded at Honeysuckle Creek, which was the prime station for LM audio after the handover from Goldstone at 112:00:00 . Colin notes that the quality is much better than the NASA archives copies and that, in the HSK recording, the voices of the people working near McCandless in the MOCR are very clear.] MP3 Clip ( 0 min 48 sec )

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Okay. RCS (Reaction Control System, the steering jets) Alpha is 81 percent; RCS Bravo, 75 percent. Coming up on 115 hours GET, descent oxygen is 31.8 pounds or 59 percent; descent amp hours 858 (remaining), and ascent amp hours 574. Over. (Pause)

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Copy. Thank you very much.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Out. (Long Pause) Tranquility, this is Houston. We also have a set of about 10 questions relating to observations you made, things you may have seen during the EVA. You can either discuss a little later on this evening or sometime later in the mission at your option. How do you feel? Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: I guess we can take a couple of them up now.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: McCandless
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Okay. And your friendly Green Team here has pretty well been relieved by your friendly Maroon Team, and I'll put Owen on with the questions. (Pause) [Astronaut Owen Garriott takes over as CapCom for the EVA debriefing.]

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Garriott
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Tranquility...

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Okay. Thank you, Bruce. If you...(Listens) Go ahead.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Garriott
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Tranquility, Houston. First question here is how your best estimate of the yaw of the LM as compared to the nominal pre-flight plan. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: (Sounding congested) We're yawed 13 degrees left on the ball, and I think that's probably about right. Looking at the shadow and so on, we're probably about 13 degrees left of the shadow.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Garriott
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. That's 13 degrees left of the shadow. [That is, the spacecraft is facing about 13 degrees south of west.] [Aldrin, from the 1969 Technical Debrief - "I want to inject a thought about spacecraft location (probably means 'orientation') in respect to lunar surface working conditions. Putting the area of the MESA in shadow also put the (TV) cable in the shadow. The white cable, being covered with a little bit of this powdery stuff and being in the shadow, was very difficult to observe. Consideration should be given to keeping any cable or small object out in sunlight whenever possible. It l

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Garriott
a11a1134623-1145426.text: And, next question relates to the depth of the bulk sampling that you obtained near the first part of the EVA and any changes in composition that you might have observed during the bulk sampling interval. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: I'm not sure I understand that question, but we got a good bit of the ground mass in the bulk sample plus a sizable number of selected rock fragments of different types. (Pause)

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Garriott
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger, Neil. One of the implications here is the depth from which the bulk sample was collected. Did you manage to get down there several inches or nearer the surface? Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: We've got some down from as much as 3 inches. In the area where I was looking at variation with depth in the bulk sample, there really wasn't appreciable difference, and I didn't run into any hard pan. Later on, or at some other times and other areas, why, I'd get down just a short distance, an inch or two, and couldn't go any further.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Garriott
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Believe we understand down as deep as 3 inches, did not hit any hard bed, and no significant changes in composition to that depth. Next question. The second SRC was packed rather hurriedly due to the time limitation, and wonder if you would be able to provide any more detailed description of the samples which were included in the second SRC. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1134623-1145426.text: We got two core tubes and the solar wind and about half of a big sample bag full of assorted rocks which I picked up hurriedly from around the area. I tried to get as many representative types as I could.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Garriott
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger, Neil. Next topic here relates to the rays which emanate from the DPS (Descent Propulsion System) engine burning area. We're wondering if the rays emanating from beneath the engine are any darker or lighter than the surrounding surface. Over. (Pause)

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1134623-1145426.text: The ones that I saw back in the aft end of the spacecraft appeared to be a good bit darker. Of course, as viewed from the aft end, why, they did have the Sun shining directly on them. It seemed as though the material had been baked somewhat and also scattered in a radially-outward direction, but in that particular area, this feature didn't extend more than about 2, maybe 3 feet, from the skirt of the engine. Over.

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Garriott
a11a1134623-1145426.text: Roger. Understand that near the aft end - out to the east - that the rays did appear darker. I understand, Buzz, that these were... (that) this was the appearance of the material which had been uncovered by the rays that appeared darker for 2 or 3 feet extending outward. Is that correct?

a11a1134623-1145426.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1134623-1145426.text: No. I wouldn't say it was necessarily material that had been uncovered. I think some of the material might have been baked or in some way caused to be more cohesive and perhaps flow together in some way. I don't know. Now, in other areas, before we started trampling around out front, why, we could see that (some) small erosion had taken place in a radially-outward direction; but it had left no significant mark on the surface other than just having eroded it away. Now, it was different right under the skirt itself. It seems as though the surface had been baked in a streak fashion, and I think a

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. [Comm Break]

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Columbia and Tranquility Base, this is Houston. In case you haven't noticed, the MSFN relay is not activated, so I can go ahead and relay anything if you want to talk directly.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Collins
a11a1221840-1230620.text: (Static) Columbia. Rog. (Pause)

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Houston, Tranquility. Be advised we've got...

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Collins
a11a1221840-1230620.text: (Garbled) on schedule.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1221840-1230620.text: ...(garbled under Mike) flags showing red right now. We just put a Verb 77 in. I believe that this is (garbled) (Pause)

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Tranquility Base, Houston. We've got a lot of static down here. Could you say again?

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. We have four out of eight (garbled) talkbacks indicating red. We still have the circuit breakers out as of right now. I believe this is normal. We have just entered Verb 77 on page Surface-52 and are ready to proceed with the hot fire. Is it normal to have these four red flags? Over. (Pause) [Talkbacks are little windows over the switches that show status. The window would contain either a grey square indicating normal status or a pattern of diagonal red stripes - called the barber pole - indicated abnormal or temporary status. A photo by Frank O'Brien shows RCS switches and talkbacks i

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. They are reset. [Aldrin, from the 1969 Technical Debrief - "We did an abbreviated RCS check. Because one of them was a cold-fire check, we got all the red flags coming on."]

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Columbia; Columbia; Houston. Request P00 and Accept, and we'll send some state vectors up to you.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Collins
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Okay; going P00 and Accept. [Long Comm Break; static clears. Buzz is about to start the final P57 on checklist page Sur-55 .] RealAudio Clip ( 10 min 16 sec )

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Houston, Tranquility. I used Capella in the last sighting (that is, for the P57 he did prior to 122:17:10), and it's a good ways near the edge. A good ways away from the center of detent 4 . I'm wondering if it would pay any to use Alpheratz, star number 1. It might be a little closer. However, it would delay things a little, since I'd have to designate the radar out of the way. Over. (Pause) [Buzz is indicating that the rendezvous radar is partially blocking the AOT detent he would use to observe Alpheratz and wants to know if Houston thinks it would be advisable to move the radar out of the

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Tranquility. Roger. We copy. Stand by 1. And, break, break, Columbia. We're having a little trouble getting the stuff in there (that is, the state vector into the CSM computer). Request high gain, pitch minus 20, yaw plus 150. Over. (Long Pause) And, Tranquility, Houston. We'd prefer to save the time; press on with Capella. Over.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. (Pause)

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: And, Tranquility, Houston. The RCS check looked mighty fine to us.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1221840-1230620.text: It looked good up here. (Pause)

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Columbia; Columbia; Houston. Over. (No answer; long pause) Columbia, Houston. Over. (Long Pause) Columbia, Houston in the blind. High gain: pitch minus 20, yaw plus 150. (Long Pause)

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Houston, Tranquility. Could you give me the TIG portion of the ascent Pad so I can load it in for a P57? Over.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Tranquility. Roger. Stand by one. We want to wait on that P57 until about TIG minus 50 minutes. Over.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. (Long Pause) [Aldrin, from the 1969 Technical Debrief - "We started to do the (final) P57 (on Sur-55 ) and realized that this would be too soon before lift-off (TIG = Time of Ignition). It seems to me (that) we had a time period in which we were essentially standing by."] [The P57 is scheduled for launch minus 45 minutes or 123:38 and, apparently, Houston has no interest in getting an hour ahead of the timeline. They will read up the Ascent Pad in about 5 minutes, as per checklist.]

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Columbia, Columbia, Houston. Over. (Long Pause) Columbia; Columbia; Houston. Over. [Comm Break]

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Houston, Tranquility. It turns out that detent 4 isn't usable anyway with the yaw that we have, because the Earth appears in both detent 2 and detent 3.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Tranquility Base, Houston. Roger. (Long Pause) Columbia, Houston. Over. (Long Pause) Tranquility, Houston. I have your LM ascent and CSI data Pads when you are ready to copy.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1221840-1230620.text: We're ready to copy. [They are at the middle of checklist page Sur-54 . Because Buzz is busy with the AOT, Neil will copy the LM ascent pad. However, to do so, he has the Data Card Book in one hand and a felt-tipped pen in the other. Neil's not on Vox, so Buzz makes the call to Houston for him.]

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. LM ascent Pad: TIG, 124:22:00:00; Noun 76, 55349, 00322, plus 0017; DEDA 47, plus 37104, minus 70470, plus 58604, plus 56936. Your LM weight 10837. Your T14 (is) 126, plus 20, plus 12. Over. [If, for some reason, they miss the planned launch opportunity, T14 would be the launch opportunity for the next CSM pass over the landing site. ]

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1221840-1230620.text: What's...Say again the crossrange in Noun 76.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. Your crossrange for Noun 76...By the way, we may update this later, but now it is plus 0017. Over.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. Readback follows. TIG 124:22:0000, 55349, 00322, plus 0017, plus 37104, minus 70470, plus 58604, plus 56936. LM weight 10837. T14, 126:20:12. Go.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Tranquility, Houston. Roger. Your readback correct. Now I have your CSI Pad.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Going to CSI Pad.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. CSI Pad. TIG of CSI 125:19:3470; TIG of TPI 126:57:0000; Noun 81, 0532 plus 0000; FDAI, NA; DEDA 373, 03196; DEDA 275, 04170; Noun 86 plus 0532, plus 0000, plus 0012. Tranquility, readback.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1221840-1230620.text: CSI Apollo Pad follows. TIG 125:19:3470; TIG of TPI 126:57:0000; Noun 81, 0532, plus all zeroes; 373, 03196; 275, 04170; Noun 86 plus 0532, plus 0000, plus 0012. Go.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Tranquility Base, Houston. Your readback is correct. (Pause) And, Tranquility, no need for any Gyro compensation. It's Go.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. Understand. (Pause) [The Gyro Compensation step is just above "122:53" on checklist page Sur-54 .] RealAudio Clip ( 6 min 48 sec )

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Columbia, Houston. Over. (Pause) Columbia, Houston in the blind. Request high gain. Pitch minus 30, yaw plus 170. Over. (Long Pause)

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Collins
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Houston, Columbia on the high gain. Over.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Ah! Roger, Columbia. We still need to finish your (state vector) uplink there, and then I have your CSI and TPI times and also the lift-off.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Collins
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Go ahead. Ready to copy.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. LM ascent lift-off time: 124:22:0000. Your CSI TIG, (I) say again CSI TIG: 125:19:3470. Your TIG of TPI: 126:57 0000. And the LM's Noun 81 values for CSI: 0532 - that's 53.2 for Delta VX; Delta VY all zeros. Columbia, Houston. Over.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Collins
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. I readback lift-off TIG 124:22 even, CSI 125:19:3470; TPI 126:57 even; the LM's Noun 81 for CSI, 53.2 Delta VX. Over.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Columbia, Houston. Roger. Your readback correct. (Long Pause) Columbia, Houston. We're coming up with your second load now.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Collins
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger that. (Long Pause)

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Columbia, Houston. The computer is yours, and you can do your Verb 45 Enter now.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Collins
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. Going to Block and Verb 45 Enter.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. (Pause)

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Collins
a11a1221840-1230620.text: How's the Black Team today? All primed and raring to go?

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: You bet you there, Mike.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Collins
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Good (garbled). [Long Comm Break] MP3 Audio Clip (41 min 59 sec; 39 Mb) from the Public Affairs loop starting at about 123:05:43. Clip courtesy John Stoll, ACR Senior Technician at NASA Johnson.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Columbia, Houston. About 3 minutes to LOS, and I have your consumables update.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Collins
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Ready to copy.

a11a1221840-1230620.speaker: Evans
a11a1221840-1230620.text: Roger. At 123 plus 00, RCS total minus 7 percent, Alpha minus 12 percent, Bravo plus 4.5, Charlie minus 7, Delta minus 6.5. Your hydrogen total minus 1.4 pounds; oxygen plus 1.7. Over.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Columbia, Houston. About 3 minutes to LOS, and I have your consumables update.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Collins
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Ready to copy.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. At 123 plus 00, RCS total minus 7 percent, Alpha minus 12 percent, Bravo plus 4.5, Charlie minus 7, Delta minus 6.5. Your hydrogen total minus 1.4 pounds; oxygen plus 1.7. Over.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Collins
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Whoever figured those hydrogens and oxygens out a couple of days ago must have known what he was doing.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Okay. I think I read that oxygen (wrong), it's a plus seventeen pounds.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Collins
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. Still close.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. (Long Pause) [Unlike the reports on LM consumables, which are given in terms of percentage remaining, this CSM report seems to be in terms of deviations from the expected quantities remaining (or used) at this point in the mission. Jim Lovell, the commander of the backup crew joins the conversation.]

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Lovell
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Eagle and Columbia, this is the backup crew. Our congratulations for yesterday's performance, and our prayers are with you for the rendezvous. Over.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Thank you, Jim.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Thank you, Jim.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Collins
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Glad to have all you big-room-full-of-people looking over our shoulders.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1230543-1234747.text: We had a lot of help down there, Jim. [Comm Break] RealAudio Clip ( 12 min 50 sec )

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1230543-1234747.text: And, Houston, Tranquility Base is going to give you a few comments with regard to the geology question of last night. We are landed in a relatively smooth crater field of elongate secondary...(correcting himself) circular secondary craters, most of which have raised rims irrespective of their size. That's not universally true. There are a few of the smaller craters around which do not have a discernible rim. The ground mass throughout the area is a very fine sand to a silt. I'd say the thing that would be most like it on Earth is powdered graphite. Immersed in this ground mass are a wide varie

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Tranquility, Houston. Roger. Very fine description. [Neil and Buzz probably do not realize just how compact the soil can be below a few inches depth and are mistaking the resistance of that very compact soil for buried rocks.]

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1230543-1234747.text: I suspect this boulder field may have some of its origin with this large, sharp-edged, blocky-rim crater (West Crater) that we passed over in final descent. Now, yesterday I said that was about the size of a football field, and I have to admit it was a little hard to measure coming in. But I thought that it might just fit in the Astrodome as we came by it. And the rocks in the vicinity of this blocky rim crater are much larger than these in this area. Some (boulders on the rim of West Crater) are 10 feet or so and perhaps bigger, and they are very thickly populated out to about one crater diam

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Tranquility Base, Houston. We copy. Thank you very much. (Pause) And, Tranquility Base, we're through with the ranging. You can take your S-band function switch to Off/Reset.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. 123:14:45 Evans: And, Tranquility, I have a LM consumables update for you.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. Ready to copy.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Okay. At plus 123 plus 00, RCS Alpha 78, (repeating) seventy eight percent, PQMD; Bravo is 76 percent PQMD; descent O 2 is 62, sixty-two percent. Descent ampere hours are 590...590 remaining; ascent ampere hours are 574, 574 remaining. Over.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. Copy. Sounds very good. Thank you.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. [Comm Break] [Journal Contributor Henry Spencer provides the following description of the Propellant Quantity Measuring Device (PQMD) that was part of the Reaction Control System (RCS): "The PQMD system is actually a bit complex, which may be why it got this acronym. What's sensed is the pressure/temperature ratio of the helium tank used to pressurize the propellants, which is directly proportional to the mass of the gas remaining in the helium tank. Knowing how much helium was in the system to start with, that gives the mass of helium in the propellant tanks. The propellant-tank pressu

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Tranquility Base, Houston.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Go ahead, Houston.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. For your P57 here, we did a little looking around, and it looks like Sirius and Rigel out at detent 6 would be real good on that. The Sun angle on Sirius is about 43 degrees, and on Rigel, it's about 55 degrees. Over.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger, Houston. The only trouble is that the Sun is in number 5, the closed one. And it appears to also be close enough to detent 6 to shine on the far side of the cone. And it completely obscures detent 6. I'm unable to use that at all.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Okay. We understand it now. Thank you. [Comm Break] 123:20:43 Evans: Tranquility, Houston. For your information, the circuitry looks real fine on that ascent-engine-arm circuit breaker.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. I don't think I could get it out now if I wanted to.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. We copy. [This is the breaker seventh from the left in second row of Buzz's circuit breaker panel (CB(16)), that he broke with his PLSS and reported at 112:56:28 . Buzz undoubtedly closed the breaker while performing the configuration changes indicated on Sur-47 , reporting after the mission that he used a felt-tipped pen to do so. See, also, a high-quality image of the Apollo 12 Controls and Displays .]

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: And it looks like, in detent 6 , I can pick up Venus right at the fringe, but I can't get anything else.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. (Long Pause)

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1230543-1234747.text: And by the way, Houston, our EVA antenna did retract.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Ah; roger. Mighty fine. Thank you. [Comm Break. The EVA antenna provided a radio link with the PLSS antennas. It was located on the top of the spacecraft and was raised and lowered with a T-handle mounted in the cabin ceiling.] [Armstrong - "It seems to me that it interfered with the docking. It was in the docking geometry volume."] [Aldrin - "But how would we know it was retracted - if it's up there in the top somewhere? Oh, well. We're not going to build another one of those (LM's again), I don't think."] [Although the antenna is on the top of the LM, it is at the back and would not have bee

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Tranquility, Houston.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. Go ahead.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. It looks like you're going to have to re-position the radar here (to do the star sighting for the final P57 platform alignment). We suggest you may want to start your TIG-minus-45 minute point in the checklist at about TIG minus 50. Over.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. Why do you think I need to move the radar?

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Well, we thought that you probably wouldn't be able to get the star there. (Pause)

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: On the rear detents , the radar can be pointing plus-X, and I'll be using right-rear detent. That's okay.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. That's fine then. [Comm Break. Plus-X is straight up and the right-rear detent points northeast.]

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Tranquility Base, Houston. I have one more late checklist change there on the rendezvous radar position for lift-off. Over. It's on page Surface-57.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. Go ahead.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Okay. On Surface-57 there on your Verb 21 Noun 73 trunnion , leave it 180; the shaft we'd like 335. Over.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. Understand. Shaft 335.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. And if the steerable (high-gain antenna) doesn't quite hack it on lift-off, looks like the forward Omni is good for about 30 to 60 seconds after lift-off. And then the aft Omni antenna is good for the rest of the ascent. Over.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. Copy. (Long Pause) Houston, we've got two angles here at 3 minutes in ascent. Would you confirm those? Pitch 134 and yaw minus 32. Over. (Pause)

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Tranquility Base. Roger. We verify; those are correct. [Comm Break]

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Tranquility Base, Houston.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Go ahead.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger. Eagle's looking real fine to us down here. We have a fairly high confidence that we know the position of the LM. However, it is possible that we may have a plane change; but, in the worst case, it would be up to 30 feet per second. And, of course, we don't expect that at all.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Okay. (Pause) [Houston will get tracking data starting at lift-off and, if they decide that the LM is significantly north or south of the Command Module ground track, they would have to correct the LM orbit appropriately. A 30 fps velocity change is small compared with the 5000 fps speed they must achieve to reach orbit.] RealAudio Clip ( 8 min 46 sec )

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Houston, Tranquility Base. Since we've still got plenty of time I think I'll go ahead and recycle on this 604.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Tranquility. Roger. That's okay with us, and we assume that the primary canister is still aboard. Is this correct?

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: We have one primary canister on board and one secondary. The other primary is, oh, out in front of the plus-Z pad. Over.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Rog. We copy. Thank you. [Comm Break]

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1230543-1234747.text: (Faintly in the background) Ready for the blue bag...

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: (To Houston) The PGNS looks consistent today.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Hey, that's affirmative, by gosh. Looking great. [Very Long Comm Break. Buzz's next transmission may relate to the step "06 05" which is just below center on Sur-56 . With telemetry, Houston has been able to follow along through the procedures.]

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Houston, did you copy Noun 05, and are you looking at 93? Over.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Tranquility Base. It's beautiful.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Okay. We'll proceed. [Journal Contributor Thomas Schwagmeier suggests that means that he will push the Pro(ceed) button on the DSKY to start the 'gyro torquing' that comes at the end of the 06 93 lines on Sur-56 .]

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: Roger.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1230543-1234747.text: I know where the star is; I'm not sure the PGNS knows where gravity is.

a11a1230543-1234747.speaker: Evans
a11a1230543-1234747.text: (Chuckles) Okay. [Long Comm Break. Buzz's next transmission may be related to the changed radar pointing angles on page Sur-57 .] MP3 Audio Clip (43 min 16 sec; 40 Mb) from the Public Affairs loop starting at about 123:47:47. Clip courtesy John Stoll, ACR Senior Technician at NASA Johnson.

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Houston, these are your angles, not ours.

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Evans
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger, Tranquility.

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1234747-1243113.text: And I'm standing by for some change or modification in the angles.

The center of West Crater is at about Juliett 0.54, 8.03, Little West Crater is at about Juliett 0.64, 7.58 and the actual landing site is at about Juliett 0.65, 7.52. Mike plotted the J.5/7.7 location on the flown copy of LAM-2 , with the notation 'Last Bst Pos Prior L/O', where 'L/O' is (LM) 'lift-off'. The distance from the LM's actual location to J.5/7.7 is about 230 meters. This lo

a11a1234747-1243113.text: Understand that it is just west of the crater which is at Juliett 0.5 and 7.7. Is that correct?

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Evans
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Columbia, Houston. That is correct. [Using a precision of 0.1, the center of West Crater is at J0.5/8.0 so J0.5/7.7 is about 300 m west from there. Ron Evans' answer to Mike's question isn't strictly correct, but it is impossible to know if this contributed to Mike's lack of success in spotting the LM shadow.]

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Collins
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Okay. Thank you, Ron. (Pause) [Aldrin - "He's talking to Collins about West Crater, so it must have been named that way prior (to the mission)."] [I haven't found a map Mike would have had with the name on it.]

a11a1234747-1243113.text: In work.

a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger. Thank you. (Long Pause) Columbia, Houston. You're still looking mighty fine to us.

a11a1234747-1243113.text: Thank you. (Long Pause) Columbia is holding inertially at lift-off attitude, my DAP is configured as per my procedures at a time of 124:02.

a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger. Columbia, was that Bravo and Delta roll? Over.

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Collins
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Columbia, affirmative.

a11a1234747-1243113.text: Go ahead.

a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger. Just a reminder here, we want to make sure you leave the rendezvous radar circuit breakers pulled (that is, open, to avoid a computer overload). However, we want the rendezvous radar mode switch in LGC, just as it is on Surface-59.

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Okay. (Long Pause)

a11a1234747-1243113.text: Tranquility Base, Houston.

a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger. Go ahead.

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Evans
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger. Our guidance recommendation is PGNS, and you're cleared for takeoff.

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger. Understand. We're number 1 on the runway.

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Evans
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger. (Long Pause)

a11a1234747-1243113.text: Houston, Tranquility. We're not sure that we got number 2 tank to fire. It's still showing a high pressure. [They are pressurizing the fuel tanks in the ascent stage, as per the steps near the middle of Sur-60 . The valves connecting the helium and propellant tanks are opened with small explosive charges . Apparently, they are getting a high reading of the pressure in the helium tank, which should have decreased when they opened the valve to let helium flow into the propellant tank. In the checklist, "ASC" is Ascent, and "SOV" is Shut-Off Valve.]

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Evans
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger. We confirm that. Try it again.

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Okay. We'll go to number 2 this time.

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Evans
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger. We concur. (Pause)

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Aldrin

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Aldrin

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Evans
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger.

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Evans
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger. We copy and we agree. (Long Pause) [Everybody wants to be sure that the tanks pressurized properly before Neil and Buzz proceed with the step "SYS A ASC Feed 2-Open" which provides fuel from the Ascent Propulsion System tank 2 to the Reaction Control System A. They will use APS fuel until well into the lift-off to conserve the separate RCS supply. "SYS A Main SOV (Shut-Off Valve) - Close" prevents use of the RCS supply.]

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Okay. I assume we're Go for lift-off, and we'll proceed with the ascent feed.

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Evans

Over. a11a1234747-1243113.text: (Garbled) See if you can see the, er, Cat's Paw. (Pause) (Garbled, possibly "I'm") getting all the way in front of us to the mountains. a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger. (Pause)

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger. (Pause)

a11a1234747-1243113.text: Yeah I think it is (Cat's Paw), isn't it.

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1234747-1243113.text: 1500 (horizontal velocity), 185 (vertical velocity). (Long Pause)

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Evans
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Eagle, Houston. You're Go at 3 minutes. Everything's looking good.

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger. (Pause)

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Aldrin
a11a1234747-1243113.text: Right on H-dot (meaning that their vertical velocity is exactly as expected).. Coming up to...This is H-dot Max now. (Pause) [H-dot is the vertical velocity, the time derivative of altitude. At this point, they achieve their maximum climb rate. The planned initial orbit is a 10 mile by 45 mile ellipse and, at engine shutoff, lunar gravity will have slowed H-Dot to about 30 feet per second.]

a11a1234747-1243113.speaker: Armstrong
a11a1234747-1243113.text: (garbled) part of the road, right here. (Long Pause)

a11a1234747-1243113.text: Roger. (Long Pause)

a11_1255200.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1255200.text: Roger. We saw you come up over the horizon and it looks like you had a laser operating. Could you confirm that?

a11_1255200.speaker: Evans
a11_1255200.text: Eagle, Houston. Stand by. We'll check it. And, Eagle, Houston. Can you give us a burn report? [Pause.]

a11_1255200.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1255200.text: Roger. Stand by. [Long pause.]

a11_1255200.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1255200.text: Okay. The CSI burn was on scheduled time of 125:19:34.70, 51.5 feet per second was our solution. After chasing residuals a little bit, we ended up with a minus 0.2, plus 0.7, and minus 0.1. And in the AGS, at that time, we had plus 0.4, plus 0.9, and plus 0.3.

a11_1255200.speaker: Evans
a11_1255200.text: Eagle - Eagle, Houston. We copy. Any plane change? Over.

a11_1255200.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1255200.text: No. There was no plane change on CSI, and CSM had a 2.3 foot per second burn. We had a 2.9, and we elected to postpone that. Over.

a11_1255200.speaker: Evans
a11_1255200.text: Roger. We copy, Eagle. Thank you. [Pause.]

a11_1255200.speaker: Collins
a11_1255200.text: [Very weak.] Houston, how do you read Columbia now? [No answer.]

a11_1255200.speaker: Collins
a11_1255200.text: [Very weak.] Eagle, how about asking them for some High Gain angles for me, will you, please?

a11_1255200.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1255200.text: Roger, Houston, do you have some High Gain angles for Columbia? Over.

a11_1255200.speaker: Evans
a11_1255200.text: Roger, Eagle. And, Columbia, stand by. We'll have them for you shortly. [Long pause.]

a11_1255200.speaker: Evans
a11_1255200.text: Eagle, Houston. Could you verify you switched lithium hydroxide canisters? Over.

a11_1255200.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1255200.text: That's affirmative. We started getting an erratic indication on primary, so we switched to secondary, and it was again erratic, and I thought it might have been a sensor. But it's settled down now, and we're on the secondary. Over.

a11_1255200.speaker: Evans
a11_1255200.text: Roger. We copy. Mighty fine. [Pause.]

a11_1255200.speaker: Evans
a11_1255200.text: Columbia and Eagle. Request Omni Delta for Columbia.

a11_1255200.speaker: Collins
a11_1255200.text: [Very weak.] Roger, Houston. I've been in Delta the whole time but it doesn't seem to be working. [Garble.]

a11_1260320.speaker: Collins
a11_1260320.text: [Very weak.] Eagle, are you ready to copy [garble].

a11_1260320.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1260320.text: This is Apollo Control. Columbia's now in an orbit measuring 56.6 nautical miles [104.8 km] by 62.5 nautical miles [115.8 km], and the displays here in Mission Control show the range from Eagle to Columbia a tad over 100 nautical miles [185 km] and about 99 feet per second [30.2 m/s] closure rate.

a11_1260320.speaker: Evans
a11_1260320.text: Eagle, Houston. At your convenience, we'd like to go ahead and try your lithium hydroxides on the primary and let us take a look at it down here. [Long pause.]

a11_1260320.speaker: Collins
a11_1260320.text: [Very weak.] Eagle, Tell them [garble] loud and clear since AOS [garble].

a11_1260320.speaker: Armstrong
a11_1260320.text: Houston, Eagle. Columbia's been reading you loud and clear on his Omnis, but he hasn't had any luck at transmitting to you.

a11_1260320.speaker: Evans
a11_1260320.text: Roger, Eagle. Mighty fine. We don't hear Columbia though.

a11_1260727.speaker: Collins
a11_1260727.text: [Very weak.] [Garble] burning [garble] at this point?

a11_1260727.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1260727.text: We're burning ours, Mike. Minus 1.8. [Long pause.]

a11_1260727.speaker: Evans
a11_1260727.text: Eagle, Houston. At your convenience [garble].

a11_1260727.speaker: Evans
a11_1260727.text: Columbia, Houston. At your convenience you can go to Reacq [garble] on the High Gain, and we should get you.

a11_1260727.speaker: Collins
a11_1260727.text: [Very weak.] [Garble.] [Long pause.]

a11_1260727.speaker: Evans
a11_1260727.text: Columbia, Houston. Over.

a11_1260727.speaker: Collins
a11_1260727.text: [Very weak.] [Garble.]

a11_1260727.speaker: Evans
a11_1260727.text: Columbia, Houston. You can go ahead and go to Reacq in the High Gain. We should get you then.

a11_1260727.speaker: Collins
a11_1260727.text: [Very weak.] Houston [garble.]

a11_1260727.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1260727.text: Do you have some angles for him, Houston?

a11_1260727.speaker: Evans
a11_1260727.text: Roger. Pitch minus 30, yaw 180, for Columbia.

a11_1260727.speaker: Collins
a11_1260727.text: [Very weak.] Copy. Thank you.

a11_1260727.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1260727.text: Okay. And what was your CSI - CDH solution, Mike?

a11_1260727.speaker: Collins
a11_1260727.text: [Very weak.] [Garble] 44 [garble] .6. Correction [garble] .4 and 14.6. Over.

a11_1260727.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1260727.text: Rog. Copy. Thanks. [Long pause.]

a11_1260727.speaker: Armstrong
a11_1260727.text: And, Houston, Eagle. Got an ECS light and a CO 2 light. Partial pressure's reading about one-half millimeter.

a11_1260727.speaker: Evans
a11_1260727.text: Eagle and Columbia, Houston. Roger. We copy. [Long pause.]

a11_1260727.speaker: Collins
a11_1260727.text: Houston, how do you read Columbia now?

a11_1260727.speaker: Evans
a11_1260727.text: Columbia, Houston. Go. [Long pause.]

a11_1260727.speaker: Evans
a11_1260727.text: Eagle, Houston. We're sure that's a sensor problem. You can leave it on Primary.

a11_1260727.speaker: Armstrong
a11_1260727.text: Okay. [Pause.]

a11_1260727.speaker: Armstrong
a11_1260727.text: Roger. We pulled the circuit breaker.

a11_1260727.speaker: Evans
a11_1260727.text: Roger, Eagle. [Long pause.]

a11_1260727.speaker: Armstrong
a11_1260727.text: And our water separator apparently isn't working too well. We're getting a lot of water through the suit loop, and we've changed water separators, but it doesn't seem to have improved the situation any. [Pause.]

a11_1260727.speaker: Evans
a11_1260727.text: Eagle, Houston. Roger. We copy. [Long pause.]

a11_1260727.speaker: Collins
a11_1260727.text: Eagle, Columbia. Standing by to back you up on the burn. Just let me know how it's going.

a11_1260727.speaker: Armstrong
a11_1260727.text: Okay.

a11_1260727.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1260727.text: Okay. You want to know what our Noun 81 is?

a11_1260727.speaker: Collins
a11_1260727.text: Ready to copy.

a11_1260727.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1260727.text: Okay. I think you already got the burn time - minus 8.1 [fps, -2.5 m/s], minus 1.8 [-0.5], minus 18.2 [-5.5].

a11_1260727.speaker: Collins
a11_1260727.text: Okay. That's pretty close agreement. And, for burn time, I still have 126:17:46.

a11_1260727.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1260727.text: Rog. [Long pause.]

a11_1260727.speaker: Evans
a11_1260727.text: Eagle, Houston. For a warm feeling, we're - we are agreeing with your CDH.

a11_1260727.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1260727.text: Congratulations. [Long pause.]

a11_1260727.speaker: Aldrin
