a11_1944842.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1944842.text: We confirm separation now from on-the-ground readings, from telemetry. We can confirm separation.

a11_1944842.speaker: Evans
a11_1944842.text: Apollo 11, Houston. You're still looking mighty fine here. You're cleared for landing.

a11_1944842.speaker: Collins
a11_1944842.text: We appreciate that, Ron. Thank you.

a11_1944842.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1944842.text: Altitude; 1,288 nautical miles [2,385 km]. Velocity; 31,232 feet per second [9,520 m/s].

a11_1944842.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1944842.text: And Flight Director Milt Windler has just informed recovery: Quote, "We're on final for the carrier."

a11_1944842.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1944842.text: Houston, we got the Service Module going by. A little high and a little bit to the right.

a11_1944842.speaker: Collins
a11_1944842.text: And it's rotating just like it should be. Thrusters are firing.

a11_1944842.speaker: Evans
a11_1944842.text: Good. It's got a lot of gas there to burn out, too.

a11_1945440.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1945440.text: Houston, we got the Service Module going by. A little high and a little bit to the right.

a11_1945440.speaker: Evans
a11_1945440.text: Roger. Thank you.

a11_1945440.speaker: Collins
a11_1945440.text: And it's rotating just like it should be. Thrusters are firing.

a11_1945440.speaker: Evans
a11_1945440.text: Good. It's got a lot of gas there to burn out, too.

a11_1945440.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1945440.text: It's coming across now from right to left.

a11_1945440.speaker: Evans
a11_1945440.text: Houston. Roger.

a11_1945440.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1945440.text: 800 nautical miles [1,500 km] high. Velocity; 33,000 feet per second [10,000 m/s].

a11_1945440.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1945440.text: Guidance reports Apollo 11 right down the middle of the corridor. 7 minutes away from entry.

a11_1945440.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1945440.text: Houston, Apollo 11. You going to turn on the tape recorder shortly?

a11_1945440.speaker: Evans
a11_1945440.text: 11, Houston. You can go ahead and turn it on.

a11_1945440.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1945440.text: Okay. I'll have to go to Command Reset to do that.

a11_1945440.speaker: Evans
a11_1945440.text: 11, Houston. That's negative. All you have to do is turn it on. That'll be fine.

a11_1945440.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1945440.text: I guess I don't know how to turn it on, then. I got PCM/Analog, Record, Forward, High bit rate and barber pole.

a11_1945440.speaker: Evans
a11_1945440.text: 11, Houston. We'll send the On command from down here, see if it works.

a11_1945440.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1945440.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a11_1945440.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1945440.text: Velocity; 34,630 feet per second [10,555 m/s].

a11_1945440.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1945440.text: Got our friend the Moon whipping by the field of view right now.

a11_1945440.speaker: Evans
a11_1945440.text: Roger. Copy.

a11_1945440.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1945440.text: Velocity coming up on 35,000 feet per second [10,700 m/s] now.

a11_1945440.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1945440.text: 3 minutes to entry.

a11_1945440.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1945440.text: Apollo 11 in the proper attitude and...

a11_1945440.speaker: Evans
a11_1945440.text: 11, Houston. We'll have you for about 3 or 4 minutes through Redstone and then pick you up after blackout through ARIA.

a11_1945440.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1945440.text: Roger.

a11_1945440.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1945440.text: Apollo 11 lined up right down the middle of the entry corridor. Velocity's now 35,578 feet per second [10,844 km].

a11_1945440.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1945440.text: We're a minute and 45 seconds from entry. Blackout will begin 18 seconds after entry.

a11_1945440.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1945440.text: Houston, Apollo 11. I'm going to go to Command Reset and turn the tape on.

a11_1945440.speaker: Evans
a11_1945440.text: 11, Houston. Recommend negative on that. That'll put us in low bit rate. [Pause.]

a11_1945440.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1945440.text: Okay. I already put it to Command Reset, but I still have barber pole on the tape. And now my switch is high bit rate.

a11_1945440.speaker: Evans
a11_1945440.text: Okay. That'll be fine. On 225, there, if you can reach it, Buzz, the last two circuit breakers in the second row from the bottom. Punch those in. [Pause.]

a11_1945440.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1945440.text: 36,000 feet per second [10,970 m/s].

a11_1945440.speaker: Evans
a11_1945440.text: And 11, Houston, don't mess around with that 225 there.

a11_1945440.speaker: Aldrin
a11_1945440.text: Okay. [Long pause.]

a11_1945440.speaker: Evans
a11_1945440.text: And 11, Houston. You're going over the hill there shortly. You're looking mighty fine to us.

a11_1945440.speaker: Armstrong
a11_1945440.text: See you later.

a11_1945440.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1945440.text: We're at entry time. Blackout very shortly. Range to go to splash 1,533 nautical miles [2,839 km].

a11_1945440.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1945440.text: There's blackout.

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:04:10 - The elapsed time for end of blackout; 195 hours, 7 minutes even.

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:04:42 - Drogue chute deployment time is 195 hours, 12 minutes, 8 seconds.

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:04:58 - And the Control Center will not attempt to communicate with Apollo 11 after drogue deploy time. It'll leave the airwaves clear for the recovery forces.

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:06:03 - ARIA 3 reported a visual contact.

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:06:26 - We're at 3 minutes, 20 seconds since entry. Blackout should end about 3 minutes, 53 seconds after entry.

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:06:59 - We're about 11 minutes away from landing.

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:07:07 - ARIA 3 would - is the up-range ARIA aircraft.

a11_1950336.speaker: Evans
a11_1950336.text: Apollo 11, Houston through ARIA. [No answer.]

a11_1950336.speaker: Evans
a11_1950336.text: Apollo 11, Houston through ARIA. [No answer.]

a11_1950336.speaker: Evans
a11_1950336.text: Apollo 11, Houston through ARIA 4. [No answer.]

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:08:47 - The Hornet reports Air Boss 1 has visual contact.

a11_1950336.speaker: Evans
a11_1950336.text: Apollo 11, Houston through ARIA. Standing by. Over. [No answer.]

a11_1950336.speaker: Evans
a11_1950336.text: Apollo 11, Houston in the blind. Air Boss has the visual contact. [No answer.]

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:09:58 - The Hornet now reports a visual contact. Visual contact from the recovery ship.

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:10:37 - Hornet reports momentary visual contact has now disappeared behind clouds.

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:10:49 - We're 7 minutes, 44 seconds from entry [meaning after entry began]. Drogue chute deployment scheduled for an elapsed time from entry of 9 minutes, 1 second.

a11_1950336.speaker: Evans
a11_1950336.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Standing by for your DSKY reading. Over. [No answer.]

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:11:22 - Hawaii Rescue 2 reports an S-band contact with the spacecraft.

a11_1950336.speaker: Evans
a11_1950336.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Stand by for your miss distance. Over. [No answer.]

a11_1950336.speaker: Evans
a11_1950336.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Standing by for your DSKY reading. Over. [No answer.]

a11_1950336.speaker: Evans
a11_1950336.text: Drogues. [Long pause.]

a11_1950336.speaker: Evans
a11_1950336.text: Apollo 11, Houston. Your DSKY reading, please. Over.

a11_1950336.speaker: Armstrong
a11_1950336.text: Roger. We were aiming right on 13, 32 and 169, 17. [Long pause.]

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:12:48 - Apollo 11 reports right on. We take that to mean that the drogues deployed on time.

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:13:22 - Apollo 11 should be on main chutes now.

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:13:35 - Hornet reports a sonic boom a short time ago.

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: 195:14:08 - We're just under 4 minutes to landing.

a11_1950336.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1950336.text: We will continue to monitor for any conversation between the spacecraft and recovery forces, but we will not initiate a call from now on to the spacecraft from the Control Center.

a11_1951503.speaker: Hornet
a11_1951503.text: Apollo 11, Apollo 11. This is Hornet. Hornet. Over.

a11_1951503.speaker: Armstrong
a11_1951503.text: Hello, Hornet. This is Apollo 11 reading you loud and clear. Our position 13, 30; 169, 15.

a11_1951503.speaker: Hornet
a11_1951503.text: 11, Hornet. Copy 13, 30; 167, 5. Any further data? Over.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Hornet has voice contact. Aircraft reports visual with 3 full chutes.

a11_1951503.speaker: Hornet
a11_1951503.text: Do you have an error?

a11_1951503.speaker: Hornet
a11_1951503.text: We have that. And what is condition of the crew?

a11_1951503.speaker: Hornet
a11_1951503.text: 11, this is Hornet. What's your error of splashdown and condition of crew? Over.

a11_1951503.speaker: Armstrong
a11_1951503.text: The condition of crew [garble]. 4,000 - 3,500 feet, on the way down.

a11_1951503.speaker: Hornet
a11_1951503.text: 11, this is Hornet. Copy. 11, Hornet. What's your splashdown error? Over.

a11_1951503.speaker: Armstrong
a11_1951503.text: Okay. Our splashdown error is by latitude, longitude, 13, 30; 169, 15. That's [garble].

a11_1951503.speaker: Hornet
a11_1951503.text: Hornet. Roger, out. [Long pause.]

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Hornet reports spacecraft right on target point.

a11_1951503.speaker: Armstrong
a11_1951503.text: Okay, Hornet. Apollo 11 is out.

a11_1951503.speaker: Hornet
a11_1951503.text: Roger. 2,500 on chutes. [Pause.]

a11_1951503.speaker: Swim 1
a11_1951503.text: Swim 1 has [garble] contact, bearing 150, holding [garble] 190.

a11_1951503.speaker: Hornet
a11_1951503.text: Hornet. Roger. Out.

a11_1951503.speaker: Swim 1
a11_1951503.text: [Garble] bearing 200.

a11_1951503.speaker: Armstrong
a11_1951503.text: Apollo 11 at 1,500 feet.

a11_1951503.speaker: Hornet
a11_1951503.text: Hornet. Roger. Copy. Out.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: That's Neil Armstrong giving the position report.

a11_1951503.speaker: Swim 1
a11_1951503.text: Swim 1 has a visual. Dead ahead about a mile and a half? [Garble].

a11_1951503.speaker: Hornet
a11_1951503.text: Hornet. Roger.

a11_1951503.speaker: Swim 1
a11_1951503.text: We're in sight of the spacecraft.

a11_1951503.speaker: Swim 1
a11_1951503.text: Roger. This is Swim One, Apollo 11.

a11_1951503.speaker: Armstrong
a11_1951503.text: [Garble] 100 feet.

a11_1951503.speaker: Swim 1
a11_1951503.text: Roger. You're looking real good. [Long pause.]

a11_1951503.speaker: Swim 1
a11_1951503.text: Splashdown! Apollo has splashdown.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Stable 2 is upside down. The flotation bags will right the spacecraft.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: It normally takes 8 to 10 minutes for the flotation bags to right the spacecraft. Swim 1 is getting ready to deploy swimmers.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Apollo 11 reported still in stable 2, but gradually righting itself.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Apollo 11 is stable 1 now, stable 1.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Swimmers to deploy in about 1 minute.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The sea anchor has been deployed by the swimmer.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: 3 swimmers in the water from Swim 2, Swim 2 Helo.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The crew has reported to Air Boss that they are in excellent condition. Flotation collar is about half way around the spacecraft now.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The flotation collar is attached now.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: And the collar is inflated.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Air boss reporting the spacecraft riding very smoothly.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Recovery 1 getting ready to deploy the swimmer with the biological isolation garments. The other swimmers...

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The swimmer with the Biological Isolation Garments is in the raft next to the spacecraft. That's Lt. Clancy Hatleberg of Chippawaw Falls, Wisconsin. He's also wearing a Biological Isolation Garment.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: And the helo is lowering the astronauts' BIGs, or Biological Isolation Garments, to Lt. Hatleberg.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: And the report is that the bag of BIGs is in raft number 2.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: That was Mike Collins reporting the crew was excellent.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Lt. Hatleberg putting on his Biological Isolation Garment.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The ship reports it is now 7 miles from the spacecraft.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Unofficial splash time: 195 hours, 18 minutes, 21 seconds.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Hornet reports the other swimmers are now up-wind of the Command Module leaving Lt. Hatleberg in his BIG and with the decontaminant that will be placed around the hatch and on the...

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Lt. Hatleberg is now transferring the BIGs to the crew.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The Hornet now estimates they are 4 and three-quarters miles away from the spacecraft.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The BIGs are in the Command Module and the hatch has been closed again.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Lt. Hatleberg is called the BIG swimmer.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The BIG swimmer is now spraying the hatch area and the top deck and around the hatch on the Command Module with the decontaminant.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The Hornet advises the crew they're 4 miles away.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Hornet reports it was 13 miles from the aim point at splash. The carrier was 13 miles from the aim point at splash.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The BIG swimmer has reported communicating with the astronauts by visual hand signals through the hatch window.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The first astronaut is now emerging.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Astronaut number 2 coming up the hatch now.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: And the third crewmen is out of the spacecraft now.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Hatch is closed and secured.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Hornet now reports that the swimmer is having some difficulty securing the hatch and one of the astronauts is helping him.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Hatch is now reported secure.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Hornet now 1 and one-quarter miles from the spacecraft.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: And the Lt. Hatleberg spraying decontaminant around the hatch.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: And the swimmer now scrubbing down the Command Module with the decontaminant.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The swimmer has now started scrubbing the astronauts' biological isolations garments with the decontaminate.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Hornet estimates distance three-quarters of a mile now.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: And the first astronaut has been scrubbed down and the swimmer has started the decontamination processes on the BIG of the second astronaut.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Scrub down on the second astronaut completed.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: And the third astronaut has been scrubbed down, and now the astronauts are scrubbing down the swimmer.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The other swimmers will now proceed to the Command Module. It has been decontaminated, and the swimmers will remain on their scuba air.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: And Recovery 1 going in now to pick up the first astronaut.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: Mission Director George Hage has just thanked the flight controllers assembled here in the Control Center on behalf of himself and General Phillips for the way in which they conducted this mission.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: No cigars being lit up here yet. We're waiting until the crew is on the carrier. A few are being wetted in anticipation of a match, but we don't see any lit yet.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The elevator will take Recovery 1 down to the hangar deck and where the crew will enter the Mobile Quarantine Facility. And the flags are waving and the cigars are being lit up. And clear across the big board in front is President John F. Kennedy's message to Congress of May, 1961: I believe that this nation should commit itself to achieving the goal, before this decade is out, of landing a man on the Moon and returning him safely to Earth. That has been accomplished.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: The Apollo 11 plaque has been hung in the Mission Control Center - a replica of the crew patch.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: This Control Center becoming jammed with people as - people from the staff support rooms coming in here. We've never seen this many people in the Control Center at one time before.

a11_1951503.speaker: Mission Control
a11_1951503.text: This is Apollo Control. The participants in the post-recovery news conference have left the Control Center, and the post-recovery news conference will begin within the next few minutes in the MSC building 1 auditorium.
